entries.title: @oxy.so/db 1.6.0
entries.content:
### `entityIdParam`: one route-param guard for entity ids

`entityIdParam(name | names, { status })` is an Express middleware (typed
structurally, no `express` dependency) that answers `{ error: { code, message } }`
when a route param is not a live entity id (`isLiveEntityId`: legacy 24-hex or
uuid v7). `status` is `400` (default, `bad_request`) or `404` (`not_found`) for
routes that must not distinguish a malformed id from a missing row. It replaces
the hand-rolled `if (!isLiveEntityId(id)) return ...` guards. Additive.

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 6.9.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- An app without NativeWind starts Metro again. The Bloom single-instance
  resolver called the resolver it wrapped without checking there was one; only
  NativeWind's config sets `resolver.resolveRequest` (Expo's default has none),
  so every request of an app that drops `nativewind` threw
  `parentResolveRequest is not a function` and Metro never served a bundle.
  It now hands the request to Metro's own resolver (`context.resolveRequest`)
  when it wraps none, as the preset's other resolvers already did.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler 1.5.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- An offset's axis takes points computed at render (`.offset({ y: nudge })`) and rejects a number written out with the token to write, as a frame's lengths do; the frame length `'auto'` and the stacking level `'1000'` are tokens.
- A dynamic `toElement(chain)` whose chain is host views alone, modified only by what reads nothing (the spec's `reads`) and taking no handler or ref, stays a `toElement` call: the runtime draws it as those views, with no boundary for a `LanguageRoot` to build it in. A chain with an `.onLayout()` or a `.ref()` is still built by the boundary, so the React Compiler reads them as a JSX prop.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-codemod 0.5.0
entries.content:
### Compatibility

- Its peer is `@oxy.so/bloom-language` 1.7.0 or newer, the language it writes (an offset in points, the frame length `'auto'`, the stacking level `'1000'` and a border width with no colour).

### Added

- Maps a transform of translations alone as `.offset()` (a number written out as its space token, one computed at render as points), an `aspectRatio` computed at render, `width: 'auto'` and `w-auto`/`h-auto`/`size-auto` as the frame length `'auto'` (no longer dropped: on a Bloom component it takes back the component's own length), and `zIndex: 1000`/`z-[1000]` as `.zIndex('1000')`.
- Maps `absolute` with no inset (a class or `position: 'absolute'` in a style) to `.position({})`, a view taken out of the flow where it sits, where it gave up (`absolute-without-edges`); an edge computed at render stays the position on its own.
- Maps a border width with no colour, a style's `borderWidth` (or an edge's, `borderBottomWidth`…) beside no border colour and a `border` / `border-b-2` class beside no colour class, to `.border(undefined, width, edge?)`: the line in the platform's default colour, where it was left JSX. A sample-app pill and rule join the corpus.
- Maps a `pointerEvents` in a style where it draws. A StyleSheet's style is compiled by react-native-web into the prop's classes, so it is `.allowsHitTesting()` on every platform (`none` `false`, `box-none` `'children'`, `box-only` `'self'`, `auto` `true`); in an inline object or a module style constant react-native-web writes `box-none` and `box-only` as CSS the browser drops, so it is `.when('native', (v) => v.allowsHitTesting('children'))` (or `'self'`), as Mention's attachment move row draws. An inline `none` or `auto` stays JSX with its own reason (the browser keeps it, and what is inside inherits it instead of taking the prop's rule). A style modifier can hold on one platform, a variant as a `native:` class's.
- Maps a Text's (and a span's) `onPress` and `onLongPress` to `.onPress()` and `.onLongPress()`.
- An element inside a Text that the codemod does not convert (a router's `Link`, an app's component) is an element run, `Embed(element)`, so the Text converts around it; an embedded `asChild` element around one text it converts is `Embed((render) => <Link … asChild>{render(Text(…))}</Link>)`.

### Fixed

- The child of an `asChild` element is no longer made a `toElement` root outside a language view: the element hands its child its own props (expo-router's `Link asChild`: the href and the press), which a root took in place of its host and dropped. It stays JSX, with the reason `as-child`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language 1.7.0
entries.content: ### Compatibility - Requires `@oxy.so/bloom` 23.9.1 or newer (its `BloomImage` names an image by its `alt` on the web, which `Image(source, alt)` draws through); the peer is `>=23.9.1`. ### Added - `.offset({ x, y })` takes points the view computes as it renders (`.offset({ y: nudge })`, React Native's `translateY` by a size's own amount), the geometry rule a frame, a pinned edge, a stacking order and a padding follow (spec `points.params`); a number written out stays a token. `.aspectRatio()` was a number already: a ratio computed at render (a media's own) is documented beside the written one. - Tokens: the frame length `'auto'` (a width's or a height's own size, React Native's and the web's `auto`, Tailwind's `w-auto`/`h-auto`), which takes back a Bloom component's own length for its content's (a `Field`'s full width); the stacking level `'1000'` (`z-[1000]`). - `.border(undefined, width, edge?)`: a border width in the platform's default colour (React Native's black natively, react-native-web's own on the web), as a style with a `borderWidth` and no `borderColor` draws it; a colour chosen at render may be none (`.border(subscribed ? 'border' : undefined, 'thin')`). It paints nothing from the theme, so a root or `view()` body around it reads none. ### Changed - A root whose tree is host views alone (stacks and spacers, the spec's new `reads.hostViews`) and reads nothing is those views, with no boundary fiber: a root over a bare `View` costs what the `View` does (Mention's splash marker, an empty sticker frame). A tree that comes to read something is drawn again under a boundary; one that holds a `view()`, an embedded element, a control or a list keeps its boundary whatever it reads. - A RawText reads nothing set above it (it takes no inherited trait), and the theme only when a role inks it: a lone RawText, or one in a `view()` body, costs React Native's `Text` in a component that inks it. - An Avatar's and an AvatarGroup's own props (size, shape, avatar colour, motion, presence, the group's layout and counts) read nothing where a tree starts, so a `view()` that hands its props to Bloom's Avatar costs what the component that renders it does (Mention's `AccountAvatar`: two context reads fewer). - The modifiers that read nothing where a tree starts are the spec's `reads.nothing`, one list for the runtime and the compiler. - `InlineMarkdown`'s `.plainRun()`, `.linkView()` and `.suffix()` hand back runs of the text (`TextRuns`: one run, or several in order, strings beside spans and element runs), drawn as runs of the line, so a post's linkified plain run is its prose as strings and its mentions, tags and URLs as spans, with no span around the prose. A string they returned was dropped before. ### Documented - A Card's fill is Bloom Card's `style.backgroundColor` when it is in the card's own box (after its padding and frame, before a corner), so `.background('transparent')` there draws no surface: the parity suite holds Mention's three composer cards (an article preview, an event in a row, a room) to Bloom's Card with their caller's zeroed chrome, and the cost gate holds such a card to Bloom's Card with that style. - Pressable runs and element runs inside a text: a span takes `.onPress()` and `.onLongPress()` as a nested React Native `Text` takes `onPress`, and `Embed((render) => {render(Text(…))})` hands expo-router's `Link asChild` a span's host (its href, role and press, an anchor on the web, and the Link's own `hrefAttrs` such as `rel: 'nofollow'`). Parity and the per-node cost gate measure each against the JSX it stands for. ### Fixed - A tab's selection reaches the web: a view with `.role('tab')` and `.accessibilityState({ selected })` writes the flat `aria-selected`, as an option already did, the two roles ARIA gives one. react-native-web reads no `accessibilityState`, so a tab lost its selected state there. Parity: a tab selected and not, against React Native's View with `accessibilityRole="tab"` and its `aria-selected` on the web. - `Image(source, alt)` names the image on the web (its `aria-label` and ``), as `.label()` does and React Native's Image with an `accessibilityLabel` does, with the next Bloom's `BloomImage` (which hands `alt` on to react-native-web as its `accessibilityLabel`). Parity: `parity/image-name.cases.tsx`, against React Native's Image on the web and Bloom's image natively. - The web parity harness drops what a browser drops: a `pointer-events` of `box-none` or `box-only` (react-native-web writes React Native's values as they are for a `pointerEvents` in an inline style), which jsdom kept. Layout parity holds `.when('native', (v) => v.allowsHitTesting('children'))` (and `'self'`) equal to such an inline style, and `.allowsHitTesting('children')` to a StyleSheet's, which react-native-web compiles into its prop's classes.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.9.1
entries.content: The Bloom language 1.7.0 (`@oxy.so/bloom-language`), its compiler 1.5.0 (`@oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler`) and its codemod 0.5.0 (`@oxy.so/bloom-language-codemod`) ship beside it. ### Changed - `StatBar` and `DataTable` paint through the colour tokens (`useColorTokens()`) instead of `useTheme().colors`, their tertiary text through `--faint-foreground`. Nothing draws differently. ### Fixed - `BloomImage`'s `alt` names the image on the web. Its own documentation says `alt` is the same as `accessibilityLabel`, and expo-image and React Native's native Image read it so, but on the web BloomImage draws react-native-web's Image, which reads only `accessibilityLabel`: the image wrote an empty `` and no `aria-label`. It now hands `alt` on as the `accessibilityLabel` when none is given, so the web writes both, as React Native's Image with an `accessibilityLabel` does; native draws what it drew. The Bloom language's `Image(source, alt)` names its image on the web through it.

entries.title: create-oxy-app 0.10.0
entries.content:
### Added

- `--language` writes the frontend in the Bloom language (`@oxy.so/bloom-language`) on
  Bloom without NativeWind; `--jsx` (the default) keeps the JSX frontend, and an
  interactive run asks. The language frontend's routes are `layout()` and `screen()`: an
  app shell over a stack of two tabs, a notes list read from `@oxy.so/bloom-data`, a form
  whose inputs are bindings, and a note pushed over the tabs. Its header actions are
  glass in one `GlassGroup`, one tinted. Metro is wrapped with `withBloomLanguage` and
  Jest runs `jest-expo` through the compiler's transformer, so an unknown modifier or
  token fails the tests as it fails the build; `packages/frontend/AGENTS.md` points agents
  at Bloom's language docs. It has no NativeWind, Tailwind, react-native-css, `global.css`
  or `className`, and takes its own Oxy set: Bloom `^23.0.0`, Services `^15.0.0`, Core
  `^7.49.0`, app-preset `^6.9.0`, bloom-language and its compiler `^1.0.0`, bloom-data `^0.1.0`.
- `verify-language-app.mjs` scaffolds a language app, installs it (optionally over local packs) and runs its
  typecheck and tests.

### Changed

- Templates render as layers (`base`, then `jsx` or `language`, then the optional
  `backend`, `deploy` and JSX `demo`), and two layers writing one file is an error. The JSX
  frontend's files moved from `base` to `jsx`; a JSX app renders as before.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 15.0.0
entries.content:
Services keeps its data in `@oxy.so/bloom-data`: one store per account, opened by the session, with
its own durable copy (one SQLite file per account on a device, one IndexedDB database on the web).
React Query and zustand are gone from the package. Account switching needs no cache wipe: the
runtime opens the next account's store before anybody is woken, and an answer for the account
that was left is dropped.

Services also takes Bloom 23 and leaves NativeWind: its screens style through React Native styles
and Bloom's colour tokens (`createTokenStyles` from `@oxy.so/bloom/theme`) and pass no
`className`, which Bloom 23 no longer takes. They draw as they did on Bloom 22 (each converted
element was rendered before and after, light and dark, native and web); an app needs no NativeWind,
`react-native-css` or Tailwind for Services.

### Peers

- **Added:** `@oxy.so/bloom-data` `>=0.1.0` (required; one instance per app, like Bloom) and
  `expo-sqlite` `>=58.0.0 <59.0.0` (required: each account's durable copy on a device).
- **Removed:** `@tanstack/react-query`, `@tanstack/react-query-persist-client`,
  `@tanstack/query-async-storage-persister`, `@tanstack/query-sync-storage-persister` and `zustand`.
  An app that uses React Query or zustand itself declares them itself.
- **Changed:** `@oxy.so/bloom` `>=22.1.1` becomes `>=23.0.0`.
- **Changed:** the floor is Expo SDK 58, the first SDK that ships what Bloom 23 needs
  (`react-native-reanimated` 4.6+, `react-native-gesture-handler` 3.3+): `react` `>=18.0.0 <20.0.0` becomes `>=19.2.0 <20.0.0`; `expo` and every Expo module
  peer are `>=58.0.0 <59.0.0`, `react-native` becomes
  `>=0.83.0 <0.89.0` (0.83 for react-native-macos, Astro's latest),
  `react-native-reanimated` `>=4.6.0 <5.0.0` and `react-native-gesture-handler` `>=3.3.0 <4.0.0`.
  `compat/expo-58` (was `compat/expo-54`) checks that stack, with react-native-macos 0.83.
- **Astro's macOS target stays on Services 14.** Expo SDK 58 needs React Native 0.87 entry points
  (`react-native/unstable-internals-do-not-use`, which expo-asset imports, and
  `react-native/asset-registry`) that react-native-macos 0.83, its latest release, does not ship,
  so a macOS app cannot bundle the Expo 58 stack. `compat/expo-58` still renders `<OxyProvider>` as
  macOS under Jest; its macOS Metro bundle step is dropped and comes back once react-native-macos
  0.87 or later exists.
- **Removed:** `nativewind` (optional) and `react-native-css`.
- **Unchanged:** `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` stays a required peer. Services reads
  it only to move its device key-value data into bloom-data, each key the first time it is read,
  and to delete its dead keys once (among them the 14.x query caches, `oxy_query_cache_v3` and
  every `oxy_account_queries:<account>`); `@oxy.so/core` and `@oxy.so/protocol` still load it on a
  device (the device id, the identity marker, the crypto storage), and Expo links only required
  peers.

### Removed

- Every `className` prop: `ProfileButton`, `BenefitList` and `BenefitRow` take `style` (they already
  did), and `OxyAuthScreen`'s `className` is `inSplit` (the form column of an `OxyAuthSplit`, which
  from `md` fills its half). The `className` typings Services added to React Native's `ScrollView`
  and `FlatList` are gone.
- `OxyProvider` no longer mounts a `QueryClientProvider` and takes no `queryClient` or
  `accountQueries` (also gone from `OxyRuntimeProviderProps`). An app that uses React Query mounts
  its own `QueryClientProvider` above `OxyProvider`, and invalidates its own queries on an account
  switch if it needs to; its per-account offline data belongs in bloom-data entities, which live in
  the account's store.
- `AccountQueriesConfig`, `AccountQueryMeta` and `PersistedRootBound`.
- `queryKeys`, `mutationKeys` and the invalidation helpers `invalidateAccountQueries`,
  `invalidateUserQueries`, `invalidateSessionQueries`, `invalidateDeviceQueries`,
  `invalidatePrivacyQueries`, `invalidateSecurityQueries`, `invalidateStorageQueries`,
  `invalidatePaymentsQueries`, `invalidateConnectedAppsQueries` and `invalidateAuthMethodsQueries`.
  A screen reads again with its view's `refresh()`.
- `upsertCachedUser` and `upsertCachedUsers`: `storeUsers` (below) is the one way a person joins
  the SDK's people, with `{ cleared }` as before.
- `useAuthStore`: read the signed-in account with `useOxy()` (`user`, `isAuthenticated`,
  `isLoading`) or the runtime hooks (`useActiveAccount`, `useOxySnapshot`).
- `useAssetStore` and its selector hooks `useAssetsStore`, `useAsset`, `useUploadProgress`,
  `useAssetLoading`, `useAssetErrors`, `useAssetsByApp`, `useAssetsByEntity`,
  `useAssetUsageCount` and `useIsAssetLinked`; `useAssets` keeps its shape.
- `useFollowTargetStore`; `useSeedFollowTargets` seeds follow targets instead.
- `supervisionQueryKeys`; `supervisionState` is the supervision source.
- `useUserProfiles`, `createProfileMutation`, `createGenericMutation`, `ProfileMutationConfig` and
  `GenericMutationConfig`.
- `useOxy().isAccountCacheReady`: `RequireOxyAuth` renders a signed-in subtree at once (each
  screen reads its account's data from disk as it opens), and a cached cold boot paints without
  waiting for a cache restore.

### Changed

- **Reads return bloom-data views.** Hooks keep their names and arguments.
  - `RecordView` (`value`, `isLoading`, `isFetching`, `status`, `error`, `refresh`) from
    `useCurrentUser`, `useUserById`, `useUserByUsername`, `useUserProfile`, `useUsersBySessions`,
    `useConnectedApps`, `usePrivacySettings`, `useSession`, `useSecurityInfo`,
    `useAccountStorageUsage`, `useSignInMethods`, `useAuthMethods` (`AuthMethodsView`, with
    `methods` and `did`), `useUserSubscription`, `useUserPayments`, `useUserWallet`,
    `useUserWalletTransactions`, `usePersonalPlans`, `usePersonalPlanSubscriptions` and
    `useSupervision`. The answer is `value` (was `data`); `refetch()` is `refresh()`.
  - `ListView` (`ids`, `hasMore`, `more`, `refresh`, `isLoading`, `isFetching`, `extra`) from
    `useSessions`, `useDeviceSessions`, `useUserDevices`, `useSecurityActivity`,
    `useRecentSecurityActivity` and `useInfiniteSecurityActivity`. A row is read with
    `useEntity(Session | DeviceSession | Device | SecurityEvent | Domain, id)`; a page is
    `more()` (was `fetchNextPage()`).
- **Writes return `ActionView`** (`run`, `isPending`, `error`, `data`, `reset`; `run` was
  `mutateAsync`, and there is no fire-and-forget `mutate`): `useUpdateProfile`, `useUploadAvatar`,
  `useUpdateAccountSettings`, `useUpdatePrivacySettings`, `useUpdateNotificationPreferences`,
  `useUpdateUserPreferences`, `useRevokeConnectedApp`, `useUploadFile`, `useSwitchSession`,
  `useLogoutSession`, `useLogoutAll`, `useUpdateDeviceName` and `useRemoveDevice`. A write shows
  at once (an optimistic layer) and settles with the server's answer, or drops exactly its layer
  when it fails. Offline it waits for the network.
- `useUpdateAccountSettings().run(updates)` takes the updates alone; the signed-in person is
  snapshotted when it is called.
- `useMutationStatus()` reports the signed-in account's writes (bloom-data's action status):
  `MutationStatus` keeps `pending`, `paused`, `total`, `isOffline` and `isSyncing`; `erroring` goes
  (a failed write rejects to its caller). An app's own React Query mutations are not counted.
- `useOnlineStatus()` reads bloom-data's `environment`, which `OxyProvider` feeds from NetInfo on
  native; the browser feeds it on web.
- `useFollow` reads whether the viewer follows a person, and their counts, from `User`
  (`relationship`, `_count`), so a profile read, a feed author and a follow agree. It is
  overloaded: a string gives `SingleFollowResult`, an array `MultiFollowResult`, so a caller that
  passed `id || undefined` passes the id (or `''`) to get the single-person fields.
- `clearAllAccountData()` deletes the account's bloom-data store (memory and disk) instead of
  clearing a query cache.
- A device's session rows (`DeviceSession`) refer to their person in `User`, so a profile edit
  shows on them, and in the account switcher, at once.

### Added

- `User` (the people the SDK reads, by id and by `username`), `storeUsers` and `UserRecord`.
- `Session`, `DeviceSession`, `Device`, `SecurityEvent` and `Domain`, the rows of the list
  hooks, with `DeviceSessionsExtra` and `SecurityActivityPageExtra`.
- `SIGNED_OUT_DATA_ACCOUNT`, the store key of the signed-out viewer.
- `supervisionState`, `useSeedFollowTargets` and the `AuthMethodsView` type.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.24.2
entries.content:
### Fixed

- A returning signed-in session paints from the device's cache again when this app once recorded a sign-out. The cached paint refused whenever the sign-out intent was stored, but that intent is not cleared when the device signs back in through another app, while the holder's own mint restores the session either way. Every cold boot of such an account waited for the registry classification and the mint before its first frame (Mention, Pixel 8a: about 3 s, and 6 to 7 s on a slow connection; 1.1 to 1.2 s with the paint). The intent still stops the boot from creating a session on its own, a sign-out still deletes the cached profile, and the background check still signs out a session the server ended.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler 1.4.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- Checks chains against the language 1.6.0 spec: the new modifiers, tokens and roles are accepted (among them `.textShadow()`, `.accessibilityElement()`, `.focusable()`, `.collapsable()`, `.sticky()`, `.cursor()`, Dialog's `.control()`, `.detached()` and `.panelFrame()`, the inputs' `.inputMode()`, `.inputRef()` and `.onSelectionChange()`, and an app colour's `.opacity()`), padding takes points computed at render, and a variant under a settled condition takes what the chain takes except the spec's `variants.held.except`, so `when('native', (v) => v.accessibilityHidden())` compiles.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-codemod 0.4.0
entries.content:
### Compatibility

- Its peer is `@oxy.so/bloom-language` 1.6.0 or newer, the language it writes.

### Added

- Maps the React Native props the language 1.6.0 takes: `accessible`, `tabIndex` 0 / -1, `collapsable`, a static `delayLongPress` with an `onLongPress`, a text shadow written out, `insetInline` / `insetBlock`, `sticky` with `top-0` / `bottom-0` (bare or `web:`), a `TextFieldInput`'s `textContentType`, a field's `inputMode` and `inputRef`, Search's `ref` and `onSelectionChange`, Item's `role="option"` and a view's `role`, and `{...hoverGroupProps}` as `.hoverGroup()`.
- Maps Bloom component props: Dialog's `control`, `detached` and a `panelStyle` of static frame lengths; an Avatar style that is its radius alone; AvatarGroup's `ringColor`, `variant` and a one-parameter `renderItemAction`; Avatar's and AvatarGroup's `motion`; Search's `editable`; `stickyHeaderIndices`; `Loading`'s `color` and `PageHeader`'s `scrimColor`.
- A handler or none chosen by a plain condition is mapped as written where the modifier takes `undefined`: `onEndReached`, a list's `onRefresh`, an `Item`'s `onPress`, and PageHeader's `onBack` between a handler, `undefined` and `null`.
- A padding computed at render is points; an inset read from `useContentSafeAreaInsets()` is `.safeAreaPadding(side, 'content')`; `flexShrink: 20` is `.shrink('20')`; the className table maps `cursor-*`, `shrink-[n]`, `bg-primary/5`, `bg-foreground/5` and `bg-white/5`.
- A glyph-alone render function (`(color) => <X fill={color} />`, or with a busy spinner as its other branch) is `Group(Icon(X))`; an icon's `style` of margins, and `fill="currentColor"` with its `color` as `.foreground(c)`.
- A style a component's caller hands in (`style={[styles.row, style]}`, `props.containerStyle`) is the reason `caller-style`, with the documented form.

### Fixed

- A `Pressable` whose children are a render function of its press state stays JSX (`render-children`): it wrote `Embed(({ pressed }) => …)`, but `Embed`'s function is handed the child, not the press state.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language 1.6.0
entries.content:
### Compatibility

- Requires `@oxy.so/bloom` 23.9.0 or newer (its `readThemePaint()`); the peer is `>=23.9.0`.

### Added

- React Native props as modifiers, each written on the view's outermost host as the JSX writes it: `.accessibilityElement(on)` (`accessible`), `.focusable(on)` (`tabIndex` 0 / -1), `.collapsable(on)`, `.onLongPress(action, duration)` (`delayLongPress`, with the duration `'500'`), `.sticky(edge?)` (the web's `position: sticky` at 0; native draws in place) and `.position({ horizontal, vertical })` (`insetInline` / `insetBlock`). `Text(...).textShadow(shadow)` takes the tokens `'0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.8)'` and `'0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.8)'`. `TextField(...).textContentType(type)` is iOS's content type.
- Bloom component props as modifiers. Dialog: `.control(control)` (Bloom's `useDialogControl()`; it ends the chain as `.presented()` does), `.detached()` and `.panelFrame(frame)` (Bloom's `panelStyle`); the space token `'540'`. AvatarGroup: `.ringColor(color)`, `.variant(rendition)` and `.itemAction((item, index) => view)` (Bloom's `renderItemAction`). Avatar: `.cornerRadius(radius)`. Avatar and AvatarGroup: `.motion('auto' | 'always' | 'never')`. Search: `.editable(false)`. ScrollView: `.stickyIndices(indices)`.
- A list's end action, refresh action and sticky rows chosen at render take `undefined` for none: `VirtualList(...).onEndReached(action | undefined, threshold?)`, `.stickyIndices(indices | undefined)`, `ScrollView(...).onEndReached(action | undefined)` and a `RefreshAction`'s `onRefresh`. `Row(...).onPress(undefined)` is an `Item` with no press, as Bloom draws `onPress={undefined}`.
- App colours (`defineTokens({ color })`): `SpinnerIcon().tint()`, `Loading().tint()`, `Header().scrimColor()` and a control's painted colour props take one, passed to Bloom as written. An app colour token gives itself at an opacity, as a role does (`severity.color[level].opacity('12.5')` is the hex with its alpha byte; an `rgb()` becomes an `rgba()`).
- Tokens: the opacities `'5'`, `'25'`, `'12.5'` and `'31.4'` (the last two are the hex alphas `20` and `50`); `.font('system-mono')`, the platform's monospaced face; a pinned edge at `'100%'`; a shrink rank of `'20'`; `.cursor()`, the web's pointer (`auto`, `default`, `pointer`, `grab`, `grabbing`, `text`, `move`, `not-allowed`; native has none).
- Padding takes points computed at render, the same rule as geometry (`.padding('leading', depth * 12)`); a number written out is still a token. A popover's `.alignOffset()` takes points the same way.
- `.safeAreaPadding(edge, 'content')` pads by Bloom's `useContentSafeAreaInsets()`, what the frame around the view left of the device's insets; a padding beyond it joins it on the view.
- The roles `option` and `listbox`, written as the web's `role`. A `Row`'s `.role('option')` is Bloom Item's `role="option"`, and its `.selected()` becomes `aria-selected`.
- Text inputs (Search, TextField, TextEditor): `.inputMode()`, `.inputRef(ref)` (the `TextInput`'s own ref, which a `.focused()` binding also reads; `.ref()` stays the box's) and `.onSelectionChange(fn)`.
- A variant under a settled condition (a platform, `disabled`, a boolean) takes what the chain itself takes, except a box layer, a placement, a press, a name or motion: the spec's `variants.held.except`, read by the runtime and the compiler. `when('native', (v) => v.accessibilityHidden())` hides a view from native screen readers only.
- `Button(Group(Icon(X)))` whose glyph names no ink of its own draws the glyph in the ink Bloom hands it (Bloom's `(color) => <X fill={color} />`), with no glyph box. A circle or pill whose content is one view is Bloom's icon button (`iconOnly`), so `Button(Group(busy ? Loading() : Icon(X)))` keeps its square.
- A glyph that is only placed (a margin, a flex, a pin) takes its placement as its own style, with no view around it. `currentColor` is the glyph's `color` on every platform.

### Performance

- A root (`toElement`, the compiler's root) and a `view()` body read only what their tree takes from where it is placed: the environment when a node takes a value from above (a press, a text, a glyph with no colour of its own), the theme when a node paints a theme colour. Both read through React's `use`, so a root whose tree comes to read more keeps its state. A tree of fixed geometry reads no context and needs no theme provider.

### Fixed

- A text trait under a condition that holds as the view renders (a platform, a disabled view) is the chain's own: `RawText(x).when('native', (v) => v.font('system-mono'))` wrote no font family on native, because the trait went into the live variants, which React Native's Text and a span do not read.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.9.0
entries.content:
The Bloom language 1.6.0 (`@oxy.so/bloom-language`), its compiler 1.4.0 (`@oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler`), its codemod 0.4.0 (`@oxy.so/bloom-language-codemod`) and `@oxy.so/bloom-lens` 1.2.0 ship beside it.

### Added

- The colour token `--faint-foreground` (`faintForeground` from `useColorTokens()` and `createTokenStyles`, `--color-faint-foreground` in `theme.css`, `faint-foreground` in `tokens.json` and `BloomColorScopeTokens`): the tertiary text, `theme.colors.textTertiary`'s own token. Every preset and seed holds it at `--muted-foreground`'s colour, so nothing renders differently; in `mode="adaptive"` on Android and iOS it is the platform's tertiary label (Material You `outline`, iOS `tertiaryLabel`), as `textTertiary` is, where `--muted-foreground` is the secondary one. `textTertiary` had no token, so a component reading it could not move to the tokens. An exact `muted-foreground` in a `BloomColorScope` also sets it unless the scope names `faint-foreground` too, so a scope's tertiary text keeps following its quiet text as before. The Bloom language's `textTertiary` role paints `var(--faint-foreground)` on the web.
- `readThemePaint()` (`@oxy.so/bloom/theme`): `useTheme()` and `useThemePaint()` in one read through React's `use`, not a hook, so a renderer that draws from a tree it builds reads the theme only when that tree paints from it. The Bloom language's roots and `view()` bodies read it so; the language's next release needs this Bloom.

### Changed

- Many families paint through the colour tokens (`useColorTokens()`) instead of `useTheme().colors`: rating, stepper, wizard, the stay and home search, lists, inputs, agents, chat, markdown, project board, dialog, cover header, app shell, listing editor, subscription plans, notifications, radio, data table, agent thinking, agent log, task list, web search, layout, grouped section, typography (`Text`) and page header. Nothing draws differently. On the web some `fill` attributes are now a `var(--…)` where they were the resolved `rgb()`, and the computed colour is the same.
- An icon's default fill is the `--primary` token. Outside a `BloomThemeProvider` an icon no longer throws: it fills from Bloom's default palette, as every token reader does.
- A native `reveal` drawer moves on the press, before React renders: the shell's open, close and toggle (the menu button, the veil, Back, a sidebar choice) start its open amount on the UI thread synchronously (`executeOnUIRuntimeSync`), and the state and its render follow while it moves; a controlled parent that declines slides it back. The closed drawer stays laid out (its rail at opacity 0, drawing nothing), so opening changes no layout, and the reveal's hosts are `collapsable={false}`: the page's wrapper toggled its accessibility props and Fabric moved the whole page (REMOVE and INSERT of every child) on every open and close. Mention on a Pixel 8a, 5 opens and 5 closes: from the tap to the first frame that moves, ~70–110 ms before (after an ~80 ms frame), ~19–27 ms now (the longest frame 10–16 ms); the first visible change in the screen recording from ~200–240 ms to ~35–50 ms, fully open from ~390–430 ms to ~320–370 ms; Back from ~195–230 ms to ~70–105 ms, closed from ~425–520 ms to ~355–405 ms.

### Fixed

- A covered screen's lens controls are drawn in their own place, under whatever covers them. The lens window overlay drew every resting lens above the whole window, so a screen under a modal or a covered stack scene showed its header controls, bottom bar and FAB over what covered it (Mention: Home's header over Settings opened by deep link). Bloom marks a stack scene under the top one (`StackScene`) and the app under a modal overlay (`OverlayInertBoundary`) as covered through `@oxy.so/bloom-lens` 1.2.0's `LensCover`. With an older bloom-lens, or without it, nothing changes.
- In `mode="adaptive"` on Android and iOS, `useColorTokens()` and `createTokenStyles` paint the platform's dynamic colours (Material You, iOS dynamic), as `useTheme().colors` does: the provider builds the token record and the JS theme from one palette (`buildPresetPalette`), each token taking the colour of the `theme.colors` field it feeds. The record was the preset's, so a component on the tokens kept the preset's colours there while one on `useTheme().colors` followed the platform. Light, dark and the web are unchanged. A `ColorScopeLayer` is handed the same record.
- In `mode="adaptive"`, a `BloomColorScope` that forces the mode the device is not in (`mode="dark"` on a light phone) paints that mode's preset palette through both readers. It overlaid the platform's colours, which are the device appearance's, so a forced dark scope drew light platform fills from `useTheme().colors`.
- `tokenAlpha` and `parseRgba` take a platform colour object (`PlatformColor`, an adaptive theme's colour on a device) without throwing, and return it as it is.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-lens 1.2.0
entries.content:
### Added

- `LensCover` (`covered`, `fill`): marks a screen as covered. A lens base inside a covered screen draws its lens in its own place against `fill`, as a base inside a scroll does, and the window overlay no longer draws it, so it sits under whatever covers the screen. A base keeps its own backdrop if it has one, and a screen nested inside a covered screen counts as covered too. Bloom 23.9.0 uses it for a covered stack scene and for the app under a modal.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language 1.5.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- A disabled solid `Button` or `FAB` on glass (`.glass().disabled(true)`) keeps its glass neutral. Its tone tinted the glass whatever its state, so a disabled submit read as live (Mention's composer: a blue Publicar with nothing to post); Bloom's own lens control draws its disabled paint, which is neutral, and now the two agree.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.8.1
entries.content:
The Bloom language 1.5.1 (`@oxy.so/bloom-language`) ships beside it.

### Fixed

- A stack scene (`stackSceneLayout`) is always its own native parent. Fabric mounts the children of a view that only paints (its fill, no stacking context) straight into the view above it, and the accessibility props a covered scene takes make it a stacking context: every push moved the whole covered screen from the native screen into the scene, and every Back moved it out again, each a detach and an attach of every view in it, which then recorded all of it again and rebuilt each glass control's shaders. On a Pixel 8a that was about 50 ms of each Mention post push's mount frame (Home, about a thousand views) and about as much of each Back. Covering a scene now only updates its props.

### Changed

- Every control the lens can draw takes the native lens or Bloom's own paint through one decision (`useLensFrame` and `withLens`, `floating/lens/lens-frame.tsx`): `Button`, `Button.Group`, `Surface`, `BlurIsland` and `TabBar` each wrote it. What each draws is unchanged: the lens on Android with `@oxy.so/bloom-lens` (in the page against the surface it sits on, in a floating region or for the tab bar and an island by the window), the paint on the web, iOS, Android without the lens and inside a Dialog or a BottomSheet. A `Surface` and a `Button.Group` off the lens no longer read the surface fill and the floating region they only needed on it.
- `AgentAvatar` plays its rest loop on a native surface on Android (`AvatarSurface`, `AvatarLoops`): the loop is remembered once and drawn by the view itself, waking once per frame it shows on the vsync it is due, instead of react-native-svg frames from JavaScript. Pixel 8a, Mention's idle Home with the header's Alia avatar, process CPU from 20 s to 30 s after a cold start: about 120% of a core without it, about 45% with it (the owner build, which has it: about 38%). The iOS view (`BloomAvatarSurface.swift`) comes with it and has not been compiled.

### Fixed

- A centred `PageHeader` title that does not fit centred moves toward the narrower side instead of sliding under the wider side's controls (and, under a glass control, being refracted by its lens). Each centring spacer shrinks only to its own side's width plus the gap, on native and on the web, where the start and end margins follow RTL. (#915)

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler 1.3.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- Checks chains against the language 1.5.0 spec: the CRM, music and media, and creator nodes, and the modifiers and tokens only they took, are refused, and a screen's `.replacesBottomBar()` is accepted.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language 1.5.0
entries.content:
### Compatibility

- Requires `@oxy.so/bloom` 23.8.0 or newer (its `pressHighlight`, `useTabPagerActions()` and `Screen`'s `replacesBottomBar`); the peer is `>=23.8.0`.

### Breaking

- Removed the nodes, modifiers and tokens of the CRM, music and media, and creator families Bloom 23.8.0 removes (no app imports them; see Bloom's changelog for each list): among them `ContactProfileCard`, `PipelineBoard`, `NoteCard`, `RecentHiresCard`, the player, library, lyrics, queue and track-list nodes, the creator studio's nodes and `ShareSheet`, with `.stage()`, `.liked()`, `.shuffle()`, `.volume()`, `.release()`, `.pitch()` and the other modifiers only they took.

### Added

- `.replacesBottomBar(value?)` on a screen's root: Bloom `Screen`'s `replacesBottomBar` (Bloom 23.8.0). The screen's own bar replaces the app's bottom bar, which steps aside on the UI thread from the screen's first frame without re-rendering the shell.

### Changed

- A hover group's press highlight (`.hoverGroup()` on a view that takes a press) costs the view nothing: it is Bloom's `pressHighlight`, drawn on the `Pressable` the view already is, in its tree's palette, with no component, hook, state or effect of its own. Android: the platform ripple (`android_ripple`), one object per palette. iOS: the `Pressable`'s own pressed state lights the wash under the children, and a press re-renders that `Pressable` alone. 1.3.0 drew it with a component of its own, a shared value and `SubtleHover`'s animated wash: Mention's feed row paid 9 hook slots and one component per row. The cost gate holds a pressable hover group equal to a bare press (fibers, hooks and context reads; Android in the parity suite, iOS in the unit suite). On iOS the wash clears at once on release (1.3.0 faded it over 150 ms).
- `AppLayout` reads the tab pager's actions alone (`useTabPagerActions()`), so a navigation, a pushed route included, no longer re-renders the whole shell; only the bottom bar draws the page in front. The iOS `TabView` reads its pages the same way.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-data 0.1.2
entries.content:
### Fixed

- `useList` and `useRecord` keep their arguments while their key is the same when compiled. The React Compiler dropped the memo that held them (`useMemo(() => args, [key])` became `return args`), so in the compiled `lib/` (the web, since 0.1.1) and in an app that compiles the source, every render subscribed and observed the source again: a feed asked its service in a loop. The hook that holds them is left as written (`'use no memo'`).

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.8.0
entries.content:
The Bloom language 1.5.0 (`@oxy.so/bloom-language`), its compiler 1.3.0 (`@oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler`) and `@oxy.so/bloom-data` 0.1.2 ship beside it.

### Breaking

- Removed the CRM families no app imports: `@oxy.so/bloom/contact-card`, `@oxy.so/bloom/pipeline`, `@oxy.so/bloom/lead-score`, `@oxy.so/bloom/note-card` and `@oxy.so/bloom/recent-hires-card`, their root-barrel exports and message catalogs, and their Bloom language nodes (`ContactProfileCard`, `LeadScoreCard`, `DealCard`, `PipelineColumn`, `PipelineBoard`, `NoteCard`, `NoteCardSkeleton`, `RecentHiresCard`) with the `.stage()` modifier and the `noteCardLayout` and `pipelineLayout` tokens only they took. `@oxy.so/bloom/mail-list` stays: `List`'s mail row, the mail thread and the mail composer draw with it.
- Removed the music and media families no app imports: `@oxy.so/bloom/media-card`, `@oxy.so/bloom/media-player`, `@oxy.so/bloom/music-library`, `@oxy.so/bloom/track-list`, `@oxy.so/bloom/lyrics` and `@oxy.so/bloom/queue-panel`, their root-barrel exports and message catalogs, and their Bloom language nodes (the media cards, `LyricsView`, `LyricsPreviewCard`, the player's `TransportControls`, `NowPlayingBar`, `MiniPlayer`, `FullScreenPlayer`, `PlaybackSpeedMenu`, `SleepTimerMenu`, `DevicePicker` and `ConnectBanner`, the library's `LibraryPanel`, `LibraryItem`, `SearchField`, `TopResultCard`, `SearchResultTabs`, `RecentSearches` and `BrowseGrid`, the track list's nodes, `QueuePanel`, `QueuePanelRow` and `RecentlyPlayedList`) with the modifiers and tokens only they took (`.liked()`, `.saved()`, `.downloaded()`, `.downloadedOnly()`, `.shuffle()`, `.repeat()`, `.playbackRate()`, `.volume()`, `.devicePickerOpen()`, `.lyricsActive()`, `.queueActive()`, `.selectedIds()`, `.view()`). `media-controls`, `media-header` and `media-shelf` stay.
- Removed the creator families no app imports: `@oxy.so/bloom/creator-studio` and `@oxy.so/bloom/share-sheet`, their root-barrel exports and message catalogs, and their Bloom language nodes (`AudienceOverview`, `StreamsChart`, `TopTracksTable`, `AudienceBreakdown`, `ReleaseCard`, `ReleaseStatusBadge`, `ReleaseTimeline`, `TrackUploadRow`, `TrackMetadataForm`, `ArtistChipsInput`, `IsrcField`, `CreditsEditor`, `ArtworkUploader`, `PayoutSummaryCard`, `PitchCard`, `ShareSheet`) with the modifiers and tokens only they took (`.search()`, `.release()`, `.selectedMoods()`, `.selectedGenres()`, `.pitch()`, `.metric()`).
- Removed `ComposerLoader`'s deprecated `active` prop. Pass `phase` instead: `active={x}` is `phase={x ? 'streaming' : 'idle'}`, and a loader with no `phase` still shows its light.

### Added

- `useTabPagerActions()` (`@oxy.so/bloom/tab-pager`): `useTabPager()` without `activePage`, so a component that only moves between pages (a shell's primary action, a header's button, a composer's exit) does not re-render on every navigation. `useTabPager()` changes on each one, a pushed route included: on a Pixel 8a, opening a Mention post re-rendered the whole shell, its sidebar, the tab pager and the Videos page through it before the post's screen could mount.
- `Screen`'s `replacesBottomBar`: the screen's own bar takes the place of the app's (a post's reply prompt with the tabs docked beside it). While the screen is in front the app's `BottomBar` steps aside in one cut on the UI thread, through its own presence, stays mounted and keeps its edge claim, so nothing re-renders and the screens it covers keep their geometry; the screen's bar and content sit on the window's edge. It holds from the screen's first frame, before a `bottomBar` that waits for `useScreenEntered`. Removing the shell's bar for the route instead re-rendered the whole shell and every covered screen in the push (Mention, Pixel 8a: about 60 to 80 ms of JavaScript and 12 ms of view removal per post opened). The Bloom language says it with `.replacesBottomBar()` on a screen's root.
- `pressHighlight(colors, children, lit?)` (`@oxy.so/bloom/subtle-hover`): a pressable row's pressed state on its own `Pressable`, at no cost: no hook, state, effect or component. Spread what it returns on the row's `Pressable` (`<Pressable onPress={open} {...pressHighlight(theme.colors, content)} />`). Android: the platform ripple (`android_ripple`) in `contrast50`, one object per palette; the press reaches the view as a command and the ripple animates on the render thread. iOS: the `Pressable`'s own pressed state (its children as a function of it) lights a `contrast50` wash under the children; a press re-renders that `Pressable` alone, its children the same elements. The web gets the children back (the pointer has the hover wash). `lit` false keeps the wash's slot for a row that takes no press, so its children keep their state. Unlike `usePressHighlight`, the iOS wash clears at once on release.

### Changed

- A route pushed over the tab pager no longer runs its navigator again (`useTabsWithTriggers`): only the pager and its predictive Back, which follow whether the tabs are in front, re-render for the push and for its Back. `TabPagerLayout` read the focus itself, so every push and Back re-ran the navigator hook twice (once more for the render-time revision of the Back preview), before the pushed screen could mount (Mention, Pixel 8a: about 5 ms of JavaScript per run).
- The `react` and `react-dom` peers are `>=19.0.0` (were `>=18.0.0`). `lib/` has been compiled by the React Compiler since 23.5.0 and imports `react/compiler-runtime`, which React 18 does not have, so React 18 already failed at the first import; the range now says so at install. Every Oxy app and SDK is on React 19.
- `lib/` is compiled with function outlining on, exactly Expo's options (23.5.0 to 23.7.0 turned it off for the select compositions). `verify-react-compiler.mjs` fails the build on an outlined function that uses a name only a function of its file binds.
- `Button` (web), `Avatar`, `Badge` and `GroupedSectionIcon` memoise their slot styles and hoist their static layout into StyleSheets; list rows (`ListItem`, and the conversation, mail, call and person rows) memoise their selected fill and hoist their layout styles. No rendered value changes. (#907, #908)

### Deprecated

- `usePressHighlight()`: a row pays hooks for it (iOS: a shared value, and the wash's animated style in `SubtleHover`'s `pressed`). Use `pressHighlight`. Mention's language feed row paid 9 hook slots and a component per row for it.

### Fixed

- `useScreenEntered()` is false on a pushed stack scene until its push transition ends, as documented. The pushing render reads the navigator's last committed state, which does not hold the pushed route yet, so the scene counted as one the stack started with and was entered at once: on a Pixel 8a a Mention post mounted its replies and its reply composer a frame after the push instead of after the slide.
- On native, a `scroll="auto"` screen's list runs its content under the header: the scroller that binds `useScreenScroll` pads its own content by the header's height (`contentInsets.top`) and the content box drops its top padding. The list ended at the header's foot, so every row was cut there in a hard line and nothing passed under a floating header. A list with a refresh control should pass `contentInsets.top` as its `progressViewOffset`.
- A floating header's scroll edge is Apple's: the page colour solid over the status bar, then one eased fade (smoothstep, drawn with 16 segments) across the header to nothing 12pt past its foot. It held the whole header opaque and faded only in a 12pt strip below it, which cut text passing under the header sharply at its foot (Pixel 8a). `EdgeScrim`'s smooth ramp is the same 16-segment smoothstep everywhere (a footer keeps its chrome opaque and fades in its tail).
- `SettingsSelect` and `SelectField` are components at module scope (`SettingsSelectFromParts` and `SelectFieldFromParts` take each platform's `Select` parts as a prop), not components a factory builds. The React Compiler takes the parameters of a function a component is built inside for globals, and with function outlining, the compiler's default, it moved their `renderItem` out of the factory: every `SettingsSelect` threw `SelectItem is not defined`. An app that compiles Bloom's source with Expo's compiler options (Mention's native build) now compiles them correctly.
- The web `Select` scrolls the chosen option into view in the commit that shows the list, not a frame later. (#900)
- Dismissing the `Sidebar`'s search (Escape or clear) focuses its trigger in the closing commit. (#901)
- Opening a collapsible `Search`, or a controlled `open`, focuses the field in that commit, not a frame later. (#902)
- The multi-agent chat `Marketplace`'s back button focuses the browse search in the commit that closes the detail. (#903)
- The web `Command` palette's arrow keys move the highlight (react-native-web's `TextInput` stopped the keydown before the wrapper heard it), and the highlighted row is scrolled into view in its commit. (#904)

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler 1.2.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- Checks chains against the language 1.4.0 spec: `VirtualList`'s `.itemLayout()` and `.headerFitsContent()` are accepted, and the logistics nodes and modifiers the language 1.2.0 removed are refused.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-codemod 0.3.0
entries.content:
### Compatibility

- Its peer is `@oxy.so/bloom-language` 1.4.0 or newer, the language it writes.

### Added

- A `VirtualList`'s `overrideItemLayout` is `.itemLayout(handler)`, as written, and a `ListHeaderComponentStyle` of exactly `{ flexGrow: 0, flexShrink: 0, alignSelf: 'stretch' }` (a literal or a module constant) is `.headerFitsContent()`. Any other header style stays a reason.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language 1.4.0
entries.content:
### Added

- `VirtualList(...).itemLayout(fn)`: Bloom's `overrideItemLayout`. `fn(layout, item, index, columns)` sets `layout.span`, so a full-width row (a header, a tab strip) spans a grid of `.columns()`. FlashList and the web honour it; the `FlatList` fallback gives every item one column, as Bloom's does.
- `VirtualList(...).headerFitsContent()`: the header's container is its content's height and the list's width (`ListHeaderComponentStyle`'s `flexGrow: 0, flexShrink: 0, alignSelf: 'stretch'`, one frozen object for every list), so the engine never stretches it to the viewport and a sticky row after it starts under it.
- With both, a grid list such as Mention's profile media grid is written as `VirtualList(rows, row)`. The cost gate holds a grid with these props equal to its JSX in components, hooks and context reads, per row and for the whole list.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.7.0
entries.content:
### Breaking

- Removed the commerce families no app imports: `@oxy.so/bloom/checkout-summary`, `@oxy.so/bloom/vendor-card` and `@oxy.so/bloom/order-confirmation`, their root-barrel exports and message catalogs, and their Bloom language nodes (`CheckoutSummaryRow`, `CheckoutSummary`, `CheckoutConfirm`, `VendorCard`, `OrderConfirmation`). `cart-panel`, `menu-item`, `price-breakdown`, `payment-method`, `payment-status` and `address` stay.

### Changed

- Android draws every Bloom icon as ONE native view (`BloomIconV1`): a glyph is rasterised once per size and paint for the whole process and the view draws that shared bitmap on its hardware canvas. react-native-svg mounted three views per icon and rasterised every icon again, in software on the UI thread, each time it drew. The drawing is react-native-svg's, step for step (its path parser, the `xMidYMid meet` viewBox, even-odd fill, stroke and the `gradient` tokens), and the pixels and the icon component API are unchanged. The web keeps inline SVG; iOS, and an Android binary without the view (a JavaScript-only update on an older build), keep react-native-svg. See `docs/icons.mdx`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.24.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- A sheet holds Android Back only while it is open. The surface back bridge kept its `hardwareBackPress` listener registered after the first sheet closed, and a registered listener hands Back to JavaScript under native Back ownership, so every later Back in the app waited for the JavaScript thread instead of popping natively.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language 1.3.0
entries.content:
### Compatibility

- Requires `@oxy.so/bloom` 23.6.0 or newer (its `usePressHighlight`).

### Changed

- On Android and iOS a view with `.hoverGroup()` that takes a press shows Bloom's press highlight (`usePressHighlight`): Android's ripple on its `Pressable`, iOS's wash under its children. A view whose press handler is absent, or whose press fades (`.pressFade()`), takes none. The web is unchanged.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.6.0
entries.content:
The Bloom language 1.3.0 ships beside it (`@oxy.so/bloom-language`): a `.hoverGroup()` view that takes a press shows the press highlight on Android and iOS.

### Added

- `usePressHighlight()` (`@oxy.so/bloom/subtle-hover`): a pressable row's pressed state on Android and iOS, in `contrast50`, the fill an unfilled Bloom control takes while held. Android gets the platform ripple, bounded by the row (`android_ripple`): the press reaches the view as a command and the ripple animates on the render thread, with no React render. On iOS the press sets a shared value that the row's `SubtleHover` reads (`<SubtleHover pressed={…} />`): the wash lights on the press and fades out over 150 ms on release, on the UI thread. The web keeps the pointer's hover wash. A child that takes its own press, or a scroll that takes the touch, keeps the row unlit. A feed row with only `SubtleHover` showed nothing on native until its navigation landed, about 600 ms after the tap on a Pixel 8a.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-codemod 0.2.1
entries.content:
### Changed

- A `VirtualList`'s `stickyHeaderIndices` is `.stickyIndices()`. A row arrow that returns `toElement(chain)` is that chain, so the language draws each row with no boundary of its own.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language 1.2.0
entries.content:
### Breaking

- Removed the logistics nodes no app wrote, with Bloom's families: `CarrierQuoteCard`, `CarrierQuoteList`, `EarningsSummary`, `EarningsBreakdown`, `EarningsPayoutRow`, `JobCard`, `JobBoard`, `SignaturePad`, `ProofOfDelivery`, `VehiclePicker`, `ShipmentLoadPicker`, `ShipmentOptionsList`, `ShipmentRequestForm`, `DeliverySlotDays`, `DeliverySlotOption` and `DeliverySlotPicker`, and the modifiers only they took (`.strokeWidth()`, `.day()`, `.filtersOpen()`, `.selectedExtras()`, `.access()`, `.window()`).

### Changed

- A tree reads the theme once, where it starts: a `toElement` root (beside the environment), a `view()` body, and the content of a Bloom component that re-themes what it holds, which is a tree of its own (a dialog's content, a full-screen player's slot). Every node of it paints from that read where it is drawn. A painted node is its host with the palette's colours: it has no `Painted` leaf of its own and reads no context. A node with live variants (`Conditioned`) and one that paints the surface fill (`OnSurface`) keep their leaf, and also paint from the tree's palette.
- A drawn node records the palette it was drawn with, so a theme switch draws each tree again once. That includes a node that kept its identity and a list's rows. A `view()` body now runs again on a theme switch, as a JSX component that reads the theme does.
- A list row (`VirtualList(items, row)`) or an `Embed` render function that returns a language root (`toElement(chain)`) draws it as part of the tree, with no boundary component and no context read per row. Write a list of language rows this way, not as Bloom's JSX `VirtualList` whose `renderItem` returns `toElement(...)`.
- A root reads two contexts, the environment and the theme, where it read one before. A node that paints now adds no read, so a root with any painted node costs no more than before. A root that paints nothing costs one context read more.
- The cost gate (`parity/cost.parity.test.tsx`) measures each node against a JSX component that reads the theme once and paints by hand, and asserts that they are equal in components, hooks and context reads. It covers several painted views in one tree, a painted nested root, and a painted list row per row. A theme-switch gate (`parity/theme-switch.parity.test.tsx`) checks that a tree switched to dark draws what the same tree mounted dark draws, and that a `view()` body runs once per switch.
- A `FAB` is a squircle unless its chain names a `.shape()` (was a circle), as Bloom `Fab`'s default is, on every platform: its glass takes the 28% corner at its diameter. `.shape('circle')` keeps the capsule.
- The shell's bottom-bar FAB (`AppLayout(...).primaryAction(...)` on Android, OxyOS and the web) is Bloom's own `Fab` on no glass of the language's, the component and the paint the sidebar draws for the same action, so the two are always one colour (the accent): a tinted lens on Android, the surface tint over the frost on the web.
- An untinted glass under a solid control (a `FAB`, a `glassProminent` button) is tinted glass: on the lens the fill at 0.8 (was 0.96), Bloom's lens controls' strength, so the glass still shows through it; on iOS the system's tinted Liquid Glass, and before iOS 26 the fill at 0.8 over the blur (was opaque).

### Fixed

- A FAB's shaped glass host is cached by the host itself in a `Map`, so a host that is a string (a test's stand-in) no longer throws.

The `react-native` condition still resolves `src/`. The output imports `react/compiler-runtime` (React 19).
