entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.5.0
entries.content:
`@oxy.so/bloom-data` 0.1.1, `@oxy.so/bloom-text` 0.1.7 and `@oxy.so/bloom-editor` 0.9.1 ship beside it, compiled the same way.

### Changed

- `lib/` ships compiled by the React Compiler (1.0.0, the options Expo gives app code): apps' compiler skips node_modules, so on the web, in Node and anywhere the `import`/`require` targets resolve, Bloom's components now memoize as an app's own do (1,780 functions; the compiler leaves 316 as written, which keep their behaviour). The `react-native` condition still resolves `src/`, so native bundles are unchanged. The output imports `react/compiler-runtime`, part of React 19. `bloom-data`, `bloom-text` and `bloom-editor` ship compiled the same way; the Bloom language does not (its hosts call bodies that call hooks). The build fails when `lib/` stops being compiled (`scripts/verify-react-compiler.mjs`).
- What reads a value that changes without a re-render stays uncompiled (`'use no memo'`), since the compiler would keep the first read: the `Avatar`'s call to the image resolver (a stable resolver can return a refreshed URL for the same id), `Calendar`'s today, the web `Tooltip`'s viewport size, `useMessages` without a `LocaleProvider`, and a `Skeleton` shape's shimmer delay (read from the clock once per region).

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.3.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- A bottom toast clears the floating bottom bar again. The toast layer is an `OverlayRoot`, and its fresh bottom edge read nothing, so the stack sat on the bar; on Android the native lens drew the bar over it, and the hidden toast took every press on the bar (a persistent connection toast kept an app's tabs from opening). `OverlayRoot` takes `inheritBottomEdge`, a surface that keeps the app's bottom edge instead of a fresh one; both toast hosts set it.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-lens 1.1.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- A still lets go of its buffer without waiting for the GPU. On Android 14 and later a still is one hardware buffer drawn with no surface (`HardwareBufferRenderer`); a still drawn through a surface waited on RenderThread for the GPU to go idle when it was let go, 7 to 20 ms as a menu closed.

### Changed

- A frame of an open menu marks only the menu's area: the menu is drawn into a node bounded by what it draws, and a frame of the menu alone records only that node. The page outside the menu is not drawn again, and the glass's blur and material run only where the menu is (they ran over the whole window's damage).
- A lens that starts to sample a region the page has not changed in for half a second shows a still of it once the region has settled (50 ms): a menu opening over a page that is still samples a still from its first frames, not the page for the whole of its opening.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.3.0
entries.content:
### Added

- `BloomImage` takes `cachePolicy` (expo-image's: `memory-disk` by default, so a picture scrolled back to, or drawn again by another list row, paints in the frame it is needed instead of being decoded from disk again; `disk`, `memory`, `none`) and `recyclingKey` (a view a list reuses for another item clears the last picture at once). The web ignores both.
- The shape `Image` (`@oxy.so/bloom/shapes`) takes `placeholderColor`, the shape filled until the picture covers it, and `recyclingKey`.
- `LinkPreviewCard` takes `pending`: the preview is still being fetched, and the card is drawn at the size it will have, the cover slot and the text block both empty.

### Changed

- `Avatar` keeps its image view when its source changes and restarts its photo stages in place: a list row recycled for another person hands the same native view the new picture (cleared at once by its `recyclingKey`) instead of building a new one. Until the picture arrives the photo slot shows the theme's muted fill (`backgroundTertiary`), never a transparent hole.
- `Avatar` reads its LIVE label only when it draws the live pill: one locale context read and one hook less per avatar.
- An article `LinkPreviewCard` (one with a cover, or `pending`) holds its text block at its full shape, the site name, two lines of title and two of description: a late preview, or a title that runs to one line, does not change the card's height. A card without a cover stays compact.

### Breaking

- Removed `@oxy.so/bloom/teleport`, the vendored copy of react-native-teleport 1.2.0 that nothing imported (its native views were never in Bloom). The media flight keeps the one piece it used, the web move primitive in `media-flight/media-node.web.ts`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language 1.1.1
entries.content:
### Changed

- A language root placed straight into a language tree (`Embed(toElement(chain))`, or the root the compiler lowers `toElement` to) is drawn as part of that tree, in the environment provided at that point: it adds no component and no context read. A grid row that embeds a cell built with `toElement` paid two boundaries per cell.
- On Android and iOS a fixed colour role (`white`, `black`, `transparent`, at an opacity too: `black/half`) is drawn as its value, as Bloom's theme defines it in every scheme: no `Painted` leaf and no theme read for a style or a glyph that paints with one. The web keeps its CSS variables.
- The cost gate (`parity/cost.parity.test.tsx`) also asserts a node mounts no more components than its JSX, and covers nested roots, a fixed role at an opacity, a white glyph and a box of computed geometry.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.1.1
entries.content: The Bloom language 1.1.1 ships beside it (`@oxy.so/bloom-language`): a root nested in a language tree costs no component or context read, and a fixed colour role paints with no theme read on Android and iOS. Bloom itself is unchanged.

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 6.9.0
entries.content:
### Added

- An app without NativeWind. Bloom no longer styles with `className`, so an app
  that has moved its own `className` off (the Bloom language codemod) drops
  `nativewind` from its package.json, and `createOxyMetroConfig` then applies no
  NativeWind wrapper, no react-native-css runtime and no redirect of React
  Native's components: every `View` and `Text` is React Native's own. The
  `nativewind` option overrides the detection. `nativewind/metro` is loaded only
  for an app that uses it, and the `nativewind` and `tailwindcss` peers are
  optional.
- The base face without NativeWind: React Native's `Text` and `TextInput` files
  (react-native-web's on the web) resolve to `metro/base-font/PlainText.js` and
  `PlainTextInput.js`, the base-face hosts (`metro/base-font/hosts.*.js`, which
  NativeWind's `Text` now wraps as well). Bloom's and the language's texts name
  their family; a raw text draws Inter, or the document's family on the web.
- `baseFont` (default `true`): `createOxyMetroConfig(root, { baseFont: false })`
  leaves a React Native `Text` or `TextInput` that names no family as React
  Native draws it, the platform face (Roboto on Android, San Francisco on iOS,
  react-native-web's system stack on the web), as an app on 6.7 drew it. For an
  app whose rebuild keeps its old look (Mention's raw texts); Bloom's `Text`
  names Inter either way.

- `BloomNativeWindTheme` (`@oxy.so/app-preset/nativewind-theme`): for an app
  that takes the Bloom without NativeWind while it still has some `className`.
  Wrapped once around the app inside `BloomProvider`, it writes Bloom's colour
  tokens into react-native-css's root variables on native, as Bloom used to, and
  carries each Bloom colour scope's tokens into NativeWind's scoped variables
  (Bloom's `ColorScopeLayerContext`), so classes inside a scope follow it; the
  web needs nothing. `css/base.css` keeps importing Bloom's `theme.css`, which Bloom keeps
  for such apps until the fleet has migrated.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler 1.1.0
entries.content:
### Added

- Checks the new language's chains (its modifiers, tokens and objects, a menu section's choices) against the spec, each diagnostic linked to its docs.
- A number written out where a token goes is refused with its token as the fix; a geometry parameter (a frame, a pinned edge, a stacking order) takes points computed at render.

### Performance

- Lowers `toElement(chain)` and a `view()` body's returned chain to a root that builds them, so the React Compiler no longer bails on the component; checked against `babel-plugin-react-compiler`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-codemod 0.2.0
entries.content:
### Compatibility

- Its peer is `@oxy.so/bloom-language` 1.1.0 or newer, the language it writes.

### Added

- Converts more of an app: `TouchableOpacity` as `.pressFade()`, the accessibility state, value and live region, auto margins, a gap per axis and border lines, a style's radius, stacking level and aspect ratio by value, inset as its edges, a hit slop per side, a ref and a layout handler.
- Bloom components: a `Button`'s runtime look, glyph size, press, spinner, open state, inks and static style; a `Card`'s and a `Tabs`' style; a `Chip`'s variant, accent colour and views beside its label; a `Field` of several controls; a `DropdownMenu` tree as `Menu(trigger, ...rows).menuStyle('dropdown')`; `Fab` as `FAB(...).glass(identity)`; `PageFooter`; a `Dialog`'s `onDismissed`; a `VirtualList`'s content style, refreshing and `onRefresh`, and a `RefreshControl`, as one refresh.
- `screen()` wraps a component whose every return is a `Screen`; a padding by `useSafeAreaInsets()` as `.safeAreaPadding()`; `useColorTokens()` reads, style constants, flex triples, a `Pressable`'s pressed style as `.when('pressed')`, `StyleSheet.absoluteFill`, a text's `fontSize`, `lineHeight` and `fontWeight`, geometry computed at render as points, and React Native's edge precedence.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language 1.1.0
entries.content:
### Compatibility

- Requires `@oxy.so/bloom` 23.1.0 or newer (its floating control size and the FAB's shape geometry).

### Breaking

- An `Action`'s hit slop is the universal `.hitSlop(edge?, token)` alone: `ActionOptions` no longer takes `hitSlop` (raw insets or a number).

### Added

- Presses and accessibility: `.pressFade(opacity?)` (React Native's `TouchableOpacity` as the press host), `.accessibilityState()`, `.accessibilityValue({ min, max, now, text })`, `.liveRegion()` and `.accessibilityHidden()`.
- Layout: auto margins, `.horizontalSpacing()` and `.verticalSpacing()`, dashed and dotted borders (`.borderStyle()`), the off-scale sizes, borders, fades, corners (7, 15, 999 as `full`) and stacking levels apps write as numeric tokens, the 38 and 76 space tokens and the 96px line, an aspect ratio on any view, `.safeAreaPadding(edge?)`, a hit slop per side, `.clipped(false)`, `.contentGrows()` on a scroll and a `VirtualList`, a `VirtualList`'s `.contentMargins()` and `.spacing()`, percentages of the parent for a pinned edge, and the display face beside a numeric size (`.font('display')`).
- Geometry computed at render: a frame's lengths, a pinned view's edges and a stacking order take points besides their tokens (`spec.points`); a number written out stays a token, and the compiler refuses a literal.
- Screens: `.colorScope()`, `.keyboardAvoiding(flex?)`, `.provider()`, `.screenBackground()` and `.reselectTop()` on a screen's root.
- Menus: Bloom's dropdown everywhere (`.menuStyle('dropdown')`), sections of choices drawn as radio rows (`Section(...).selection()`), a menu the app opens (`.presented()`), and a row's and a submenu's own glyph size and ink.
- `surfaceFill`, a colour role: the fill of the surface a view sits on (Bloom's `useSurfaceFill()`), read only by the leaf that paints it.
- Views as content: a header's title and subtitle, a button's content and the views beside its label; a button's inks and spinner; a field's lines; a tab's own box and label font; a Chip's colour chosen at render; the Button, Card, Chip and Field props apps write.
- A pull to refresh as `{ refreshing, onRefresh }` (a query's `isRefetching` and `refetch`), with a tint per platform; `.ref()` and `.onLayout()` on the outermost box; `Dialog`'s `.onDismissed()`; hit testing chosen at render and a `Divider`'s own axis; a `Search`'s most characters.

### Glass

- A `Button` on glass (`.glass()`, `.style('glass' | 'glassProminent')`) is Bloom's floating size (44pt), whatever size its chain or environment names.
- `FAB(...).shape('circle' | 'rounded' | 'squircle')`: its glass takes the silhouette's corner at the FAB's diameter. A FAB is tinted with the accent by default, and on the lens a solid control's fill tints its glass at 0.96.
- On Android and OxyOS a `Menu`'s trigger is glass only when it says `.glass()` (or sits in a glass): a bare trigger (a feed row's ⋯) draws no lens, and its menu still grows out of its shape. An open lens menu frosts more than its trigger (`lensMenuBlur`).
- The web frosts a glass's backdrop as the material does.

### Changed

- `RawText` is React Native's own `Text`, writing only what its chain names: a text that names no family draws the platform face (Roboto on Android, San Francisco on iOS, the system stack on the web), not Bloom's base face.

### Performance

- `toElement(chain)` and a view body's returned chain compile to a function that builds them, so the React Compiler keeps a component that draws the language; a bare view's `toElement` stays a call, with no boundary fiber.
- A press-only `.pressScale()` holds `PressableScale`'s hooks alone; a painted leaf reads the theme once on native; a boundary reads one context (the environment carries the animation scope); a state-varied leaf subscribes to the window only for a breakpoint variant. A node costs React no more hooks or context reads than its JSX, held by a cost gate in the parity suite.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.1.0
entries.content:
The Bloom language 1.1 ships beside it: `@oxy.so/bloom-language` 1.1.0, `@oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler` 1.1.0 (and its platform packages), `@oxy.so/bloom-language-codemod` 0.2.0 and `@oxy.so/bloom-lens` 1.1.0.

### Added

- `Dialog` takes `onDismissed`: it fires once the dialog has finished closing, its exit animation done, in either mode (in controlled mode, after the host flipped `open` to `false`), the place to unmount what presented it. The language's `Dialog` takes it as `.onDismissed()`.
- The Bloom language guides ship in `docs/`: `bloom-language-getting-started.mdx` (install, the compiler in Metro, Jest and Vite, a first screen), `bloom-language-tour.mdx`, `bloom-language-from-jsx.mdx` and `bloom-language-for-agents.mdx`, every `check` example compiled by the language compiler and TypeScript in CI; and the reference generated from the language's spec, `bloom-language-nodes.mdx`, `bloom-language-modifiers.mdx` and `bloom-language-tokens.mdx`. Storybook has a `Language` section led by the tour.
- `Fab` takes `shape`: `circle` (the default), `rounded` or `squircle`, a square whose corner is 28% of the diameter, with circular or continuous corners; on the lens the glass, its press and a menu's morph take the same corner. `FAB_SHAPES`, `fabCornerRadius` and `useFabDiameter` (`@oxy.so/bloom/fab`) give the geometry to a host that draws a FAB's material itself.
- `FLOATING_CONTROL_SIZE` (`@oxy.so/bloom/button`): the one floating size, `lg` (44pt).

### Changed

- One lens path for every glass control on Android 13+ (with `@oxy.so/bloom-lens`): every `Button` and `Button.Group` with a material is drawn by the lens. In a floating region (a floating header, a toolbar, a bar, a FAB) the window draws it; anywhere else it is drawn in its place against the surface it sits on, so it scrolls and stacks with the page. A separate window (a sheet, a dialog) keeps Bloom's own material; iOS and the web are unchanged.
- Where the engine draws the glass, Bloom draws no emulated edge of its own (the extra top and bottom border is gone).
- A floating control is 44pt, decided by the control, never its caller: a `Button` or `Button.Group` on the lens (by its own prop or its region), every member of such a group, a floating `PageHeader`'s back, `leading` and `actions`, a `Button.Group` on the lens and the media header's follow toggle. `material="surface"` keeps a group on Bloom's material at its own size.
- The bottom bar is 62pt, its selected tab on a neutral translucent pill (the `shadow` token, 4pt in from the bar's wall) with accent icon and label; a FAB beside the bar takes its height.
- `Fab`'s default tone is the accent (was `action`), its glyph the accent's foreground; on the lens a solid control's fill tints its glass at 0.96.
- The web frosts a glass's backdrop as the material does.
- A floating header's back control is in the header's floating region, so it floats with the controls beside it.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-lens 1.1.0
entries.content:
### Fixed

- The glass draws no stroke outside its shape: the engine's key and fill strokes drew a line just outside the top and bottom edges, ending in a blob where the edge turns. The glass's edge is its rim and light, inside the shape (the `keyThreshold` uniform is gone).

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler 1.0.0
entries.content:
First release. The build-time optimiser for `@oxy.so/bloom-language`: a Rust pass (Oxc, through a Node addon) in front of Metro's and Jest's own transformers. It is an optimisation; the runtime interprets every chain, and the pass changes only what it proves keeps its meaning.

### Added

- Hoists static chains to module scope, including the static prefix of a dynamic chain; names resolve through scope analysis.
- Adds `"use memo"` to every function passed to `view()`.
- Checks every chain against the language spec (unknown modifiers, wrong argument counts, literal tokens outside their set) and fails the build with the source line and a suggestion.
- `withBloomLanguage(config)` from `@oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler/metro`, a Jest transformer (`/jest`) and `compile` (`/compile`).
- Prebuilt addons, so installing it needs no Rust: `@oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler-linux-x64-gnu`, `-linux-arm64-gnu`, `-darwin-x64`, `-darwin-arm64` and `-win32-x64-msvc`, as optional dependencies, and the WASI build `@oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler-wasm32-wasi` for any other platform (a musl Linux, for one), which npm installs only when asked.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language-codemod 0.1.0
entries.content:
First release. Moves an app's NativeWind `className` JSX and Bloom JSX to the Bloom language only where the rendered result stays the same, keeps everything else as JSX with its reason, and writes a report. See `docs/bloom-language-codemod.mdx` in the Bloom repository.

It is 0.x on purpose: the Bloom components it maps grow with each release, and a minor release may convert more or change a report's reasons.

### Compatibility

- Runs on Node 20.19 or newer: `npx bloom-language-codemod <app dir>` (`--help` for the options).
- Reads the language it writes for from the app's install: `@oxy.so/bloom-language` 1.0.0 or newer is its peer (the spec, the className table and the exports it ships).
- Compiles the app's NativeWind entry with Tailwind 4 from the app's own install (`tailwindcss`, `nativewind`, `@oxy.so/bloom`, `@oxy.so/app-preset`); `--package <name>=<dir>` reads one from a checkout instead.
- The parity proof (`--fixtures` and the parity suites) runs from a Bloom checkout: it renders each region with Bloom's Jest environment, the before side with Bloom 22 where the app hands a Bloom component a class.

### Added

- The CLI, `bloom-language-codemod`: the report (`report.md`, `report.generated.json`), the converted files (`--write` in place) and the parity corpus (`--fixtures`).
- A README for the npm page.
- The library entry: `transformSource`, `report`, `loadTable`, `overriddenClasses` and `tailwind`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-language 1.0.0
entries.content:
First release. Bloom's UI language: views as functions, modifiers chained in order (order means nesting), every value a Bloom token. It draws Bloom's own React Native and web components, with parity against hand-written Bloom on native and web, light and dark. See `docs/bloom-language.mdx` in the Bloom repository.

### Compatibility

- Requires `@oxy.so/bloom` 23.0.0 or newer, React 19, React Native 0.81 or newer and Reanimated 4.6 or newer. `expo-router` (for `@oxy.so/bloom-language/router`), `expo-glass-effect`, `@expo/ui` and `expo-blur` are optional peers for the platform components.
- iOS is type-checked and covered by the Jest parity suites but not yet verified on a device.

### Added

- The core: the node model, `view()`, the environment and custom modifiers, over one spec (runtime tables, the web stylesheet and the compiler's tables, generated from `spec/language.json`).
- Layout, text, icons, material and glass, buttons, avatars, inputs, platform components, navigation (`@oxy.so/bloom-language/router`), overlays and feedback, app chrome, images, containers, and Bloom's generic and product components as language nodes.
- Variants, the motion engine's modifiers and gestures, and interop with plain React Native and Bloom JSX.
- The spec (`spec/language.json`) and the className table (`codemod/classnames.generated.json`) ship with the package, for `@oxy.so/bloom-language-codemod` to read the language the app installs.
- Pair it with `@oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler` for build-time hoisting and chain checks, and with `@oxy.so/bloom-data` for data and state.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-data 0.1.0
entries.content:
First release. Bloom's data and state layer: records by id held in memory, read with field-level subscriptions, filled by sources, changed by optimistic actions and realtime events, and copied to SQLite (or IndexedDB on the web) in the background. See `docs/bloom-data.mdx` in the Bloom repository.

It is 0.x on purpose: its API is still growing (bounded persistence, source invalidation and durable actions are in progress), and a minor release may change it.

### Added

- `entity`, `list`, `source`, `action` and `realtime`, read with `useEntity`, `useList`, `useRecord` and `useListState`.
- The background copy: `@oxy.so/bloom-data/sqlite` (the `expo-sqlite` database the app passes in) and `@oxy.so/bloom-data/indexeddb`.
- React 19 is its only peer.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 23.0.0
entries.content:
Bloom's UI language ships with this major, as its own packages released from this repository: `@oxy.so/bloom-language` 1.0.0, `@oxy.so/bloom-language-compiler` 1.0.0 (with its prebuilt platform packages and WASI fallback), `@oxy.so/bloom-data` 0.1.0 and `@oxy.so/bloom-lens` 1.0.0. See `docs/bloom-language.mdx`.

### Breaking

- Bloom styles without NativeWind, react-native-css or Tailwind: every component draws React Native styles from tokens (see `docs/no-nativewind.mdx`). The look is unchanged.
  - Removed: every `className` and `*ClassName` prop (pass `style`, or the language's modifiers), `useColorScopeStyle` and `initCssInteropDarkMode`.
  - Peers removed: `nativewind` and `react-native-css`. Apps no longer need NativeWind, react-native-css, Tailwind or `@oxy.so/app-preset/base.css` for Bloom.
  - Kept for apps that still use `className` of their own, until the fleet has migrated: `./design-tokens/theme.css` and `./tailwind-preset`. On native, Bloom no longer publishes its tokens to react-native-css: such an app wraps its tree once in `BloomNativeWindTheme` from `@oxy.so/app-preset` 6.9 or newer, inside `BloomProvider`, so its classes follow the theme and each colour scope. Upgrade an app that still has `className` on native together with that app-preset.
  - Moving an app's `className` JSX to the language: the className codemod (`packages/bloom-language-codemod`, `docs/bloom-language-codemod.mdx`, `docs/bloom-language-classnames.mdx`) runs from a Bloom checkout; it is not published yet.
- Peer floors raised: `react-native-reanimated` >= 4.6.0 and `react-native-gesture-handler` >= 3.3.0. Bloom's motion engine and its gesture layer (drags, pinch, double tap; the bottom sheet, sidebar tree rows and sortable chips) are built on Gesture Handler 3.
- New optional peer `@oxy.so/bloom-lens` (>= 1.0.0): the native lens material on Android 13+. Without it Bloom keeps its own material.

### Added

- `@oxy.so/bloom/theme`: colour tokens and token styles, the one way a component paints: `useColorTokens`, `createTokenStyles`, `tokenAlpha`, `ColorToken`, `ColorTokens`, `ColorScopeLayerContext` and `ColorScopeLayer`; the `transparent`, `surfaceForeground`, `accent`, `destructive`, `white` and `black` theme colours; tone `vivid`, the brand at full strength.
- `@oxy.so/bloom/blur` publishes the blur family; `BlurIsland` draws the native lens where the device has it.
- Bloom's motion engine (`@oxy.so/bloom/motion`): springs from a velocity, motion values over shared values, delays, loops and colour transitions, exits played natively after unmount, and a gesture layer of motion values (`usePinch`, `useDoubleTap`, drags that share a scroll view's touches). The pop, the roll, the toast and press feedback run on it.
- The native lens material on Android 13+ (with `@oxy.so/bloom-lens`): `Select`, `ContextMenu` and `DropdownMenu` present as native glass; `Button material="glass"`; `Surface`, `Fab`, `TabBar`, `ButtonGroup`, `HeaderActions`, a floating `PageHeader`'s controls, `Chip`, `Badge` and the small buttons take the lens; native sheets and dialogs present in the app window.

- `BloomImage`, Bloom's raster renderer (expo-image on a device, react-native's `Image` on web), is public: `@oxy.so/bloom/image` and the root barrel export it with its prop types (`BloomImageProps`, `BloomImageSource`, `BloomImageContentFit`, `BloomImageLoadInfo`, `BloomImageErrorInfo`). See `docs/image.mdx`.
- `adoptStyleSheet(id, css)` is exported from `@oxy.so/bloom/styles`: the CSP-safe way to put CSS on a web page as a constructed stylesheet, the mechanism Bloom's web forks use.
- `useScreenActionClaimed()` is exported from `@oxy.so/bloom/app-shell/hooks`: whether the screen in front shows a primary action of its own (`Screen primaryAction`). A floating action the app draws for the shell (a bottom bar's FAB) steps aside while it is `true`, as the shell's own does, so a route with its own action never shows two.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.52.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **Oxy services act for people without permissions (ADR 0066).** An Oxy service whose first-party registry entry declares `actsForPeople` names the account it acts for and nothing else: `oxy.actingFor({ accountId, requesterAccountId? })`, `oxy.assets.actingFor(...)`, `oxy.linkedAccounts.actingFor(...)`, `createServiceClient({ actingFor })` and `oxy.agency.createFirstPartyExecutionAuthorization(terms, { requesterAccountId? })`. They send `X-Oxy-User-Id` (and `X-Oxy-Requester-Id` when the person operates the account) and strip any a caller passes; no session, task, ticket or requester context, so they work the same in the background. `serviceRequest` takes `requesterAccountId` beside `actAs`.
- **Receivers admit it with no change.** `middleware.auth()` sends the request's effect (`read` for `GET`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS`, else `write`) and `X-Oxy-Requester-Id` to Oxy's verification, and sets `req.serviceActingAs.requesterId` on a first-party answer. `verifyActingAs` accepts a first-party answer without a requester proof only with the caller's presented token, `authorized: true`, no scopes, no requester context and an exact `requesterId`.
- **`oxy.apps.firstPartyActivity(accountId?)`**: what Oxy's own services did for an account, per application, receiver, effect and day (`FirstPartyActivityEntry`).

### Deprecated

- `withRequester`, `createServiceClient({ requester })`, `agency.createTask`, `createTaskExecutionAuthorization`, `createForegroundExecutionAuthorization` and `revokeTask` for Oxy's own services: superseded by `actingFor` (ADR 0066) and removed once their last callers move.

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 6.7.3
entries.content:
### Fixed

- The base worker's offline shell failed in production (`net::ERR_FAILED` on
  an offline reload of alia.onl). It was stored from `/index.html`, which
  Cloudflare's static assets redirect to `/` (307), and Chrome refuses a
  redirected response for a navigation. The shell is now fetched from `/`, and
  any stored or served shell is rebuilt as a response that went through no
  redirect (which also repairs shells stored by 6.7.2).
- An app only worked offline from its second visit: the first one loads its
  bundles and route chunks before the worker controls the page, so none of
  them was cached. The worker now stores the bundles and CSS the shell links
  when it installs, and `oxy-sw-register.js` sends it the same-origin files the
  page loaded once it takes over (`OXY_SW_STORE`; only static same-origin
  files are stored). Verified against alia.onl in Chromium: a first visit, then
  offline, renders the app.

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 6.7.2
entries.content:
### Added

- `oxy-web-pwa --remove-sw` ships a `/sw.js` that deletes the Oxy caches and
  unregisters itself: the way to take the worker away (shipping none leaves the
  old one running).
- The registration skips the HTTP cache (`updateViaCache: 'none'`) and a page
  back in the foreground checks for a new worker at most once an hour, so an
  installed app left open picks up deploys.

### Fixed

- A deploy no longer empties the cache: its name was a hash of the export, so
  `activate` dropped the previous deploy's chunks while a tab opened before the
  deploy could still need them. The cache is now `oxy-sw-v1`, bounded at 150
  entries oldest first; `activate` drops other `oxy-sw-*` caches.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.51.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`startEcosystemTraffic` in `@oxy.so/core/server`: one call to start a service's ecosystem activity.** About twenty apps each carried a near-identical wrapper around `createEcosystemTraffic` (env parsing, region gate, `installFetch`, a module singleton with a pass-through middleware, a socket observer and a stop function). The call takes `service`, `ready` and optionally `workloadCredentials`, `baseURL`, `location`, `onError`/`onRecover`, `deployedOnly` and `env`, and returns an `EcosystemTraffic` handle that is inert when the process does not publish. `OXY_ECOSYSTEM_ACTIVITY_ENABLED` (`true`/`false`, anything else throws) wins; unset, it publishes where `AWS_REGION` (else `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`) is set, or with `deployedOnly` only where the process can attest its workload identity. New type exports `EcosystemTraffic` and `StartEcosystemTrafficOptions`. `createEcosystemTraffic` is unchanged.

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 6.7.1
entries.content:
### Added

- `oxy-web-pwa --theme-color=<light>,<dark>` writes the startup `theme-color`
  as a pair scoped by `prefers-color-scheme`, the shape Bloom adopts and owns at
  runtime, instead of the manifest's single `theme_color` (a brand accent such
  as Alia's would otherwise colour the browser bar until the app hydrates).

### Fixed

- The base worker served no offline shell: it skipped every request with
  `credentials: 'include'`, and every navigation has that mode, so an offline
  reload got the browser's error page. The rule protected nothing (a
  same-origin request sends cookies under `same-origin` too); private responses
  stay out through the same-origin, `Authorization`, `/api/` and
  `private`/`no-store` rules.

entries.title: @oxy.so/app-preset 6.7.0
entries.content:
### Added

- `oxy-web-pwa <dist>`: makes an Expo web export installable. With
  `web.output: 'single'` Expo ignores `app/+html.tsx`, so the manifest link most
  Oxy apps wrote there never reached the page and no browser offered to install
  them. Run after `expo export`, the step fails the build on a manifest browsers
  refuse (or icons the export lacks), adds the manifest link, Apple tags,
  `theme-color` and the worker registration to every exported page that lacks
  them, and ships the Oxy base service worker. See README "Installable web apps".
- `web/oxy-sw-base.js`: the shared service worker, from Inbosh's: network-first
  navigation with an offline shell, stale-while-revalidate for same-origin
  hashed files, and nothing private or cross-origin ever stored. Apps with their
  own worker import it with `importScripts('/oxy-sw-base.js')`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.50.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`receiverSendsNoStore` on `OxyConfig` and `createLinkedClient`: CORS preflights that are cached.** Every request went out with `cache: 'no-store'`, so the browser's HTTP cache could never hand one account's response to another. Chromium also skips the CORS preflight cache for a `no-store` (or `no-cache`, `reload`) request, whatever `Access-Control-Max-Age` the receiver sends: every bearer request from a web app went out twice (measured in Chromium: 3 OPTIONS for 3 GETs with `no-store`, 1 with `default`; Gemies' API saw one OPTIONS per GET). A backend whose every response carries `Cache-Control: no-store` can now say so; its linked client uses the default cache mode, the browser still stores nothing, and the preflight is reused. Defaults to `false`: nothing changes for a client that does not opt in.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.20.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`accountQueries.dataVersion`: a persisted cache that survives deploys.** Both persisted caches were dropped on every new build (`OXY_BUILD_ID`), so the first visit after each deploy was cold for everyone, and apps that deploy several times a day were cold most of the time. An app may now declare the version of the data it persists; a blob is then dropped only when that version, or this package's (it owns the shape of the shared roots and of the blob), changes. Without it nothing changes: the stamp stays the build, so every app that does not opt in keeps today's behaviour. `SERVICES_PERSISTED_DATA_VERSION` is kept equal to the package version by a test.
- **`accountQueries.bounds`: caps for a root that grows with use.** `{ [root]: { maxQueries, trim? } }` writes only the root's `maxQueries` most recently updated queries, each through `trim` (for example, a conversation's last messages), gives restored data its type back with `revive` (the blob is JSON, so a `Date` comes back as a string), and removes unwatched ones past the cap from memory. `PersistedRootBound` is exported with `AccountQueriesConfig`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/contracts 6.27.0
entries.content:
Additive only: no export removed.

### Added — `oxyAccountIdCheck` in `@oxy.so/contracts/client`

- The Zod-free twin of `oxyAccountIdSchema` (1–64 characters, branded `OxyAccountId`), tied to it
  by the parity test. A client needs an `OxyAccountId` to start a product checkout
  (`expectedSubjectAccountId`), and the only way to get one was to parse through the root entry,
  which linked every schema and Zod into the app: in Gemies' and Alia's web bundles that one
  import was 984 KB (Zod 540 KB, the root's schemas 444 KB) of the JS every route loads first.
  `parseContract(oxyAccountIdCheck, id)` gives the same result from the client entry.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.19.3
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A persisted query stays in memory for as long as it stays on disk.** Both persisted caches write their snapshot from memory, and the client's default `gcTime` is 30 minutes, while the account cache is kept for 7 days and the shared one for 30. So any persisted query no screen had watched for half an hour was collected, dropped from the next snapshot, and the next visit to its screen (a skill, a gemie's thread, a list) waited on the network behind a skeleton instead of drawing what was cached. The roots each cache writes (the app's `accountQueries.roots`, less its memory-only ones, and the SDK's own) now default to `gcTime: Infinity`, set before restoring so hydrated queries get it too; they leave memory when the cache's own rules remove them (expiry on restore, an account switch, sign-out). Memory-only and undeclared roots keep the client's default. A query marked `meta: { persist: 'account' }` outside a declared root should set its own `gcTime`.

### Changed

  requires a `color` or `bodyColor`. A bot is painted in its account's `color` (`User.color`,
  a Bloom preset key), which Bloom 20 draws a bot account's character in, so the colour has one
  source and Gemies stores and sends its gemies' characters without a paint. `color` and
  `bodyColor` are still accepted, so a writer that sends them keeps working; a renderer that
  knows the account's colour ignores them. Their removal, with the stored paints, is a later
  major once no writer sends them.

entries.title: @oxy.so/telemetry 2.2.0
entries.content:
Additive: single sources for constants and logic that consumers each copied. No
consumer is migrated by this release and no existing behaviour changes.

### Added

- `OXY_TELEMETRY_REQUEST_HEADERS` (`X-Oxy-Activity-Id`, `X-Oxy-Edge-Region`: what
  a browser sends, for a CORS `Allow-Headers` list) and
  `OXY_TELEMETRY_EXPOSED_HEADERS` (`X-Oxy-Region`, for `Expose-Headers`), plus the
  constants `OXY_REGION_HEADER` and `OXY_SOURCE_REGION_HEADER`
  (`X-Oxy-Source-Region`, service to service, deliberately not in the request
  list). Tests pin the lists to the constants.
- `@oxy.so/telemetry/collector`: `UNOBSERVED_PATHS`, one table of unobserved
  paths where each entry declares its direction (`inbound`, `outbound` or
  `both`), and `isObservedPath(path, direction)` reading it. The collector uses it
  for both its middleware and its outbound fetch, and the inbound and outbound
  sets are exactly what they were (pinned by tests against the previous code).
- `@oxy.so/telemetry/server`: `sourceRegionFromEdgePop(pop)`, the one `edge-<pop>`
  derivation, now used by the collector middleware and the socket/WebSocket
  observers.
- `@oxy.so/telemetry/metrics`: `createEmfPublisherIfDeployed(options, env?)`,
  `null` unless `ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4` is set.
- Root entry types: `TrafficScope`, `TrafficDirection`, `TrafficType`,
  `TrafficFlow`, `TrafficAggregate` (the API's strict activity-batch schema),
  `InfrastructureNode` and `InfrastructureSnapshot` (the `platform_infrastructure`
  socket payload). The collector entry re-exports the traffic types unchanged.
- `fixtures/emf-golden.json` and its test: the cross-language EMF conformance
  fixture Kaana's Go `internal/emf` must also pass (see the README).

### Fixed

- `ActivityAggregate` was stale (`direction: 'inbound'` only, no scope, type or
  service fields). It is now `TrafficAggregate & { activeClients: number }`,
  the exact `platform_activity` socket payload. Nothing in any Oxy repo imports it.

### Candidates to unify in a deliberate follow-up (needs owner decision)

Not changed here. Excluded INBOUND only today, so an OUTBOUND call to them is
still recorded: `/health`, `/ready`, `/live`, `/platform-stats`,
`/platform-activity`, `/infra-status` (each with an optional `/api` prefix and
subpaths), `/platform-infrastructure/...` subpaths and `/api/platform-infrastructure`,
and `/cdn-cgi/`. The only outbound-only entry is the exact `/platform-infrastructure`.
Unifying would change what the dashboard shows (the website calls `/platform-stats`
through instrumented fetch).

### Deprecated (removal planned for the next major)

No repository under `~/Oxy` imports any of these (verified by search, including
`origin/main` of oxy): `serviceFromPath`, `activityFlow` (and `ActivityFlow`),
`ActivityCardinalityAdapter`, `presenceBucket`, `ActivityBucket`,
`DEFAULT_ACTIVE_CLIENT_WINDOW_MS`, `getBrowserTelemetryHeaders` and
`createBrowserTelemetry` (kept as a test seam until then). The README no longer
advertises them.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.19.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A query waits out a 429's `Retry-After` instead of retrying blindly.** `createQueryClient`'s retry delay is the wait the refusal named (`retryAfterSecondsOf`, the `retryAfterSeconds` of its body) rather than a 1 s / 2 s backoff that Oxy would refuse again, spending the retry budget inside the same window. A refusal that asks for more than 30 s is not held silently: the query fails at once and the screen shows it (`shouldRetryQuery`). Without a named wait the backoff is unchanged. `retryAfterSeconds` of the sign-in messages reads the same helper, so the wait it shows and the wait a query holds are one.

### Consumers

Needs `@oxy.so/core` 7.47.0.

entries.content:

Code and Codex answer "I don't have permission" to almost anything. Start it with `--read-only` to
forbid changes, and the agent then says how to lift that instead of just refusing. Run it from the

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 24.1.0
entries.content:
- **A consulted agent's reply is not drawn under its line.** When Alia or an agent asks another
  agent (`consultAgent`), the thread shows "Chatted with …" and no longer the agent's answer
  beneath it: the lead already answers the person with it, and the line opens the exchange
  (`onOpenAgentChat`) to read it. A host that passes no `onOpenAgentChat` keeps the answer where it
  was, since there would be no way to reach it. Members of a group chat are never consulted
  agents: they speak as themselves. New `consultedReplies` beside `speakerChanges`.

entries.title: @alia-codea/cli 3.3.0
entries.content:
`codea connect` serves Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode to Alia as one of your agents
([ADR 0028](../../docs/adr/0028-external-agents.md)). Create a code in Alia (Settings → Connect an
external agent), paste the text it gives you into your agent, and it runs
`codea connect --code <code> --cli <claude|codex|opencode>`. The process dials Alia outbound with your
Oxy session and answers the messages Alia sends it by running the CLI you are already signed in to, in
the current directory, read-only unless started with `--write`. Run `codea connect` again to serve the

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 24.0.1
entries.content:
- **A conversation prefetch never retries.** `prefetchConversation` (the hover/press-in warm-up)
  now fails once and quietly. It used to retry through the query client's default policy, so a
  refusal by the API's rate limit (429) was retried twice more, spending the budget that had just
  refused it; the press that opens the conversation fetches it itself.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 24.0.0
entries.content:
- **Breaking.** The web search switch is gone: Alia can always search the web, so
  `AliaTurnRequest.webSearch` (what `AliaRuntimeHost.turnRequest` returned) is removed. Hosts that
  returned it from `turnRequest`: delete it. The server still accepts `webSearch: false` from
  other clients on `/v1`.
- **Group chats.** A conversation of several agents (`memberAgentIds`, the `group` prop of
  `AliaChatContent`) gets its own welcome (`AliaGroupWelcome`, the members' avatars together), and
  the members' avatars fly out of it with the first message. Its members speak as themselves: no
  "chat with" line is drawn at each change of speaker.
- **Group rooms in real time.** The members of a group talk to each other past the request. The
  host gets a new optional hook, `AliaRuntimeHost.subscribeRoomEvents(conversationId, listener)`,
  fed from the `group:event` socket event; the thread draws a member typing, streams what the
  members write and stores their replies as they land. A host that does not implement it keeps
  today's behaviour (the request's own first round).
- **Agent threads read as a chat.** In a chat with an agent (or a group) the thread shows the
  conversation only: no "Worked for" line, task list or search trail, and the agent's tools do not
  open the thought panel on their own. Alia's own chat is unchanged.
- **"Chatted with …"** (before "Chat with …") is a button: it opens, read-only and without the
  composer, the conversation the agents had between themselves (what the calling agent asked and
  what the consulted agent answered), rebuilt from the loaded messages. The chat under it stays
  mounted and inert, so its scroll and draft survive.
- **Bubbles.** The person's own bubble has no react button (a reaction is a vote on a reply); the
  react, reply and more icons and the reaction pill are the chat reference's own.
- Built and tested against Bloom 17.39.0. The peer range stays `@oxy.so/bloom >=17.22.0`.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 23.1.0
entries.content:

  `POST /v1/conversations/:id/messages/:messageId/reactions`.
- Fix: the persisted conversation list hands its dates back as `Date`s (a hydrated list held
  `updatedAt` as an ISO string and the sidebar's sort threw `updatedAt.getTime is not a function`).
- Built and tested against Bloom 17.29.0, where the spinner of every busy state (`Loading`,
  `Button`, the send button) is the Material 3 morphing loader. The peer range stays

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 23.0.0
entries.content:
- **Breaking.** Bloom 17.22 draws characters as SVG, so the hosted 3D runtime is gone from the
  SDK. Removed: the `ALIA_CHARACTER_RUNTIME_URL` export (root and `@alia.onl/sdk/character`), the
  `characterRuntimeUrl` prop of `AliaChatSheet`, `AliaChatScreen` and `AliaSharedConversation`
  (and of `ask`), the pre-rendered still of `AliaAvatarIcon` (`bun run render:avatar-still` and its
  generated file) and the optional peer `@oxy.so/bloom-avatar-native`. The chat components mount
  Bloom's `AgentAvatarProvider` themselves. Consumers: bump to 23.0.0, delete any
  `characterRuntimeUrl` you passed and any copy of Bloom's `assets/character-runtime` you served
  (Bloom no longer ships it). `@oxy.so/bloom` is now `>=17.22.0`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.47.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **`createOxySocketCors` admits a WebSocket handshake from the server's own origin.** A native WebSocket client sends the socket URL's own origin when its caller gives none (React Native's Android WebSocketModule, iOS's SocketRocket, OxyOS), and `allowRequest` admitted only no `Origin` or an allow-listed one, so every native app's socket to a service outside the Oxy apex family was refused with `400` (OxyOS#477: Alia's realtime socket on OxyOS, Android and iOS). An `Origin` equal to the request's `Host` with the scheme of the first `X-Forwarded-Proto` value (else of the connection being TLS) is same-origin and admitted; scheme and port are part of the comparison. Every other origin keeps the allow-list rules, the opaque `null` still refused. The long-polling `cors` answer is unchanged: a same-origin request needs no CORS headers. New type `OxySocketHandshakeRequest`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.19.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- **On a session host that names the platform's languages, they are the app's language, and nothing waits for the account** (ADR 0058 R11, ADR 0022). R10 needed the account's languages in the snapshot, which a real account often lacks (the platform keeps them only after a profile read, and an account may have none): OxyOS's Dropsea still showed a blank window for 6 to 15 s on the owner's ThinkPad, waiting for the boot token and `GET /users/me`, then spoke the fallback rather than the system's language. Where the host's snapshot carries `preferredLanguages`, `currentLanguage` is the platform's from the first render, signed in or out, online or not, over the account's and the profile's; `isLanguageReady` and `isAccountLanguageKnown` are true at once and `OxyProvider`'s `language` bridge waits for neither the token, the profile, the guest override nor storage. A host without them keeps R10.
- **The language bridge shows the app in the commit that knows its language.** When the language is known at mount and the app's `language.onChange` applies it synchronously (an in-memory locale store), the bridge's children are in the same commit, so the app's first frame is its own content rather than an empty window; an asynchronous `onChange` is still awaited, and a later locale still waits for an earlier catalog.

### Consumers

Needs `@oxy.so/core` 7.47.0.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.47.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`OxyHostSnapshot.preferredLanguages`** (ADR 0058 R11): a session host may name the platform's preferred languages, primary first (OxyOS's Language & Region); where it does, they are the language every app speaks. Optional; the host contract stays 1.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.18.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **Surface header contributions** accept Bloom semantic header actions and legacy accessible-label entries. Presentation changes update the host without render loops from inline callbacks. Semantic callbacks follow stable IDs through reordering and become inert when removed; legacy static lists keep positional dispatch, and custom header nodes remain identity-compared.
- Typecheck the adapter with Bloom semantic header-action declarations while retaining support for the 17.15 minimum.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.18.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- **On a session host, the language is the snapshot's from the first render** (ADR 0058 R10, ADR 0022). When the host's snapshot carries `account.languages`, an app that passes `OxyProvider`'s `language` paints at once in that language, offline too, instead of waiting for the boot token and a `GET /users/me` (OxyOS's Dropsea waited 1.4 to 9 s for them on a slow link, and stayed blank while either could not be reached). The account is still published only with its token; it carries the snapshot's languages until the app's own profile read replaces them. A host without `languages` keeps the old behaviour.
- `useOxy().isAccountLanguageKnown`: whether the account's language is known before the session resolves (always `false` where the SDK holds the session itself).

### Consumers

Needs `@oxy.so/core` 7.46.0.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.17.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`OxySetupFlow` takes `locale`** (ADR 0064): the language its own words speak (its progress, its announcements, the default Back), a BCP 47 tag. A platform's setup passes its system's language, so the flow does not turn to the signed-in account's language halfway (the runtime follows the account once signed in, ADR 0022). `useI18n(locale?)` takes the same override. Without it, nothing changes.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.16.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`OxySetupFlow`: a platform's setup in the sign-in's own frame** (ADR 0064). A controlled, presentational multi-step frame: the host passes its `steps` (`OxySetupStep`: `id`, `title`, `description`, `icon`, `content`, `aside`, `initialFocus`, `primary`, `secondary`) and the `current` id, and owns what every action does. Each step is drawn in the SDK sign-in's shell (the icon or the Oxy mark, the 48/800 title, blocks 24 apart, 448 wide; with an `aside`, the split card from `md`, asking for 880), with Back leading and the secondary and primary actions trailing, quiet progress ("Step 2 of 5" and decorative dots), Bloom's `ScreenTransition` between steps (none under reduced motion), focus moved to the new step's title (or left to its content), and the change said politely ("Create a PIN, step 3 of 5"). `onMaxWidthChange` reports the width the current step asks, as `OxySurfaceFrame` does.
- **`oxySignInStep()`**: the SDK's sign-in as a step — `OxyAuthChooser`, unchanged, inside the flow's surface-width context, so the card grows to the QR split's 880 for that step and returns after. The host still learns the sign-in through `authStateStore` (`PlatformSetupAuthStateStore`); there is no second seam.
- `OxyAuthScreenHeader` takes `icon` (in place of the Oxy mark) and `titleRef`.

### Consumers

No API removed. Needs `@oxy.so/core` 7.45.0 (the announcement's words). OxyOS's login screen composes its setup with it.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.15.2
entries.content:
### Added

- **A platform's setup store is told how the sign-in happened.** `authStateStore.save(state, context)`: `context` is `SetupSignInContext`, `{ method: 'qr' | 'password' | 'emailCode' | 'signup', password? }`. `'qr'` is an approval from a device the person already holds (the QR, the Commons identity), passwordless, so OxyOS asks no password and its service redeems the approval for its credential (`POST /session/device/platform`, ADR 0058 R6). `'password'` carries the password just typed, after its second factor too, so the platform can reuse it once instead of asking again. Only a store the app provided receives the context; the platform's own stores never do. The SDK drops the password once the sign-in commits or fails, and never persists or logs it. `handleWebSession(session, setup?)` takes it; `PlatformSetupAuthStateStore`, `SetupSignInContext` and `SetupSignInMethod` are exported.

### Fixed

- **No route an account cannot use.** A change that needs "confirm it's you" (`ReauthStep`: set or change the password, the email, the authenticator, deleting the account) offered an account with neither an email nor a password a "current password" field for a password it does not have. It now offers neither and says the account needs an email first. An account without an email is never offered the email code (unchanged), and one with an email but no password is never asked for a password.

### Consumers

No API removed. OxyOS bumps.

entries.title: Astro preview — 30 October 2026 (macOS and Windows)
entries.content:
A test build of Astro for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Windows. It is **not signed and does not update itself**; install it to try what's new, and expect rough edges.

### What's in it
- **Sign in with Oxy**, one account for all of Astro, and your **Nilo calendar** (subscribe Google, Outlook or iCloud calendars in Nilo).
- **Chat with Alia** (Ctrl/⌘ E): the current page, @-mentioned tabs and files as context; Alia can act in your tabs with your approval, fill forms, read PDFs and Office documents, and see the tab when you allow it.
- **Skills, artifacts (reports, decks, dashboards), Morning Brief, meeting prep**, connected apps, a Library of chats and files, and dictation.
- The window is now built on Bloom: sidebar and top tab strip that hide and peek, split panes, an auto-hiding toolbar.
- First macOS build on React Native's New Architecture.

### Install
**macOS 14 or later** (Apple Silicon: `…-macos-apple-silicon.dmg`; Intel Macs, e.g. a 2018 MacBook Pro: `…-macos-intel.dmg`)
1. Open the DMG and drag Astro to Applications.
2. Open Astro once; when macOS says it can't verify it, click Done, then go to **System Settings › Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway** (or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Astro.app`).
3. If asked for the "Astro Safe Storage" keychain item, click Always Allow.

**Windows 10 or later, x64:** run `Astro-preview-2026-10-30-windows-x64-setup.exe`. It installs for your user, without an administrator.

### Known limits
- Unsigned (no Apple Team ID yet): no automatic updates, no iCloud Keychain passkeys.
- Built from `main` at `6a7d037` (rebuilt 2026-10-31: the macOS disk image and the Windows installer now carry Astro's and Oxy's name and icon).

SHA-256 checksums are in `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.8.0
entries.content:
- **Streaming dictation (ADR 0024).** `@alia.onl/sdk/dictation` gains
  `openDictationStream({ apiUrl, getToken | token, language?, onEvent, signal?, openSocket?,
  endTimeoutMs? })`: the caller's PCM16 LE mono 24 kHz frames go to
  `GET /v1/audio/transcriptions/stream`, and Alia's events come back while the person speaks:
  `dictation.ready`, `transcript.interim` / `transcript.delta` / `transcript.final` per numbered
  `segment`, `error { code, retryable }` and one `dictation.closed { reason }`. A segment's
  `transcript.final` is the only text to keep. It returns `{ append, commit, end, close, closed }`;
  `end()` resolves once the finals have arrived. The protocol module (`DICTATION_PROTOCOL_VERSION`
  1, `parseDictationServerEvent`, `dictationStreamUrl`) is exported beside it. It reaches no React
  or native module (`check:entries`). `useDictation` still records a clip for batch
  transcription; adopting the stream there is a follow-up.
- The API that serves the stream ships with this release; against an older API the socket's
  path answers 404 and the stream reports `TRANSCRIPTION_FAILED`, so batch
  `requestTranscription` stays the fallback.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.7.0
entries.content:
- **Image results for awaited host tools.** An awaited tool's `execute` may answer
  `result: { type: "image", mediaType, data, text? }` (`AliaHostImageResult`: `image/jpeg`,
  `image/png` or `image/webp`, `data` in standard base64 with no `data:` prefix, an optional
  caption of at most `HOST_IMAGE_TEXT_MAX_CHARS`, 4,000). The model sees the image itself in that
  turn; the stored conversation and the `alia.tool_result` frame keep
  `{ type, mediaType, text?, omitted: true }` instead. The whole result still counts toward
  `HOST_RESULT_MAX_CHARS` (100,000 characters as JSON), so size a screenshot to fit.
- A result that claims `type: "image"` but is malformed is answered `failed` with the reason
  (`hostImageResultProblem`), instead of being sent for the API to refuse while the model waits.
- Needs the Alia API that ships with this release (`docs/agent-embedding.md` §2); an older API
  passes an image result to the model as JSON text.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.6.0
entries.content:
- **`@alia.onl/sdk/dictation`: dictation's request on its own.** `requestTranscription`,
  `DictationError`, `dictationFailureCode`, `normalizeAudioMediaType` and `MAX_DICTATION_MS`, the
  same functions `useDictation` and `AliaComposer` use, from an entry that reaches no React, no
  native module, no recorder and no Oxy client (`check:entries` holds it). An app that records
  its own audio (Astro's browser shell) sends its clips from here instead of keeping a copy of
  the request. Nothing changes for the root entry, which still exports `requestTranscription`
  and `DictationError`.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.5.0
entries.content:
- **`AliaApi.put`.** The REST API (`useAliaApi`, `createAliaApi`) sends PUT like PATCH: the
  linked Oxy client's authentication and 401 replay, the app assertion and a JSON body. Alia's
  memory profile takes its sections by PUT (`/memory/context`, `/memory/preferences`,
  `/memory/settings`), so a host's personalization settings can save them without its own client.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.4.0
entries.content:
- **A shared conversation shows its artifacts.** `readSharedConversation` keeps an assistant
  message's `artifacts` (`AliaSharedArtifact`: `{ id, type, title, data }`, the canvas tool's
  result) and `sharedMessages` hands each to the thread as the canvas call that drew it.
  `AliaSharedConversation` draws them inline under their reply on the canvas renderers (reports,
  decks, dashboards, charts, tables). An `AliaThread` that is not `readOnly` is unchanged: in the
  app an artifact still opens in the canvas panel, not in the reply.
- The server sends `artifacts` only from the API that ships with this release
  (`docs/agent-embedding.md` §6); against an older API the shared page shows words and images,
  as before.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.3.0
entries.content:
- **Decks and dashboards on the canvas.** `CanvasComponent` draws the canvas tool's two new
  types: a `deck` (one card per slide: title, subtitle, bullets, body) and a `dashboard` (its
  stats in a row, then charts, tables and notes on the chart, table and Markdown renderers).

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.2.0
entries.content:
- **Awaited host tools.** `AliaHostToolDefinition.awaitsResult: true` declares a tool whose
  result the model reads in the same turn ("this tab's text"). When the model calls it, the
  runtime runs the host's `execute` once and POSTs `{ toolCallId, outcome, detail?, result? }` at
  once to `/v1/chat/turns/:turnId/host-results` through the authenticated API (with the app
  assertion), instead of queueing the outcome for the next request. `AliaHostOutcome.result`
  carries a string or JSON value of at most `HOST_RESULT_MAX_CHARS` (100,000) characters as JSON;
  a larger one is answered as `failed`. A failed POST is reported to `AliaHostTools.onUndelivered`
  and never retried. `parseHostAction` keeps `awaitsResult` and `turnId`.
- **Personalization off for one turn.** `AliaTurnRequest.personalization: false` (read at send
  time from `host.turnRequest()`) sends `personalization: false`: Alia reads no memory and offers
  no memory tools for that turn. Nothing is sent otherwise.
- `awaitsResult` is sent only for a tool that declares it, so existing hosts send the same bytes.
  A host that declares one needs the Alia API receiver for awaited host tools deployed first
  (`docs/agent-embedding.md` §2); an older API refuses the field with `invalid_host`.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.1.2
entries.content:
- **Every entry type-checks under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`.** The SDK ships source, so a
  consumer compiling with `"noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true` (Astro) type-checked the SDK under
  it too and got errors from indexed reads in the runtime, thread, citation and catalogue-tool
  modules (27 from `@alia.onl/sdk/runtime` alone). Each read is now narrowed where the index is
  known to be in range, with a loop over the values where that is simpler. Behaviour is unchanged.
- `check:entry-types` compiles every entry with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` on, so CI keeps it so.

entries.title: @alia-codea/cli 3.1.0
entries.content:
Ctrl+C requests authenticated Stop for the current generation and waits for its
acknowledgement before closing the stream. Every tool continuation has its own
turn ID; Stop blocks further tools, including approvals resolved late. Incidental
teardown and broken output pipes only detach. Account changes fence both lanes. Acknowledged Stop retains visible partial text
without incomplete tool calls; account teardown never saves that partial reply.

Uses the shared server SDK 1.3.1 wire parser and removes the unused OpenAI dependency.
Requires Node 22 or newer, matching the shared SDK and current CLI dependencies.

entries.title: @alia.onl/server 1.3.1
entries.content:
Preserve streamed `delta.tool_calls` as typed `tool_calls` events, including
fragmented arguments and indices, so terminal consumers can share the wire reader
without losing client-owned tools. Invalid tool fragment shapes fail explicitly.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.1.1
entries.content:
- A delayed Stop acknowledgement cannot idle a newer turn, replace its sidebar
  preview, or notify a different conversation. Thread/account changes and unmounts
  invalidate old completion callbacks while the original acknowledgement drains.
- Keep repeated Stop requests deduplicated during that drain; errors from an old
  Stop cannot appear in a replacement thread. Public APIs and peer ranges are unchanged.

entries.title: @alia.onl/server 1.3.0
entries.content:
- Add optional typed `turnId` to chat requests and `cancelTurn()` for explicit
  authenticated Stop. Aborting a stream remains transport detachment.
- Add `createAliaTurnControl()` for early IDs, deduplicated Stop acknowledgement
  and transport cleanup; callers retain their shared account fencing.
- The explicit Stop receiver must be deployed first. Supported control lanes are
  human sessions and exact app-only credentials; delegated services without a
  verified original actor retain their existing chat behavior without `turnId`.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.1.0
entries.content:
- Stop explicitly cancels the authenticated foreground turn across API replicas;
  closing a sheet or losing its transport still allows background completion.
- Export `createChatTurnControl` / `AliaChatTurnControl` from `@alia.onl/sdk/runtime`
  for custom Stop controls, with account-change fences and early-turn ids.
- Requires the explicit Stop API receiver to be deployed before adoption; see
  `docs/explicit-chat-stop.md` in the repository.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 22.0.1
entries.content:
Remove the Bloom peer upper bound to follow the first-party package policy.
The required minimum remains `15.10.1`; core `>=7.1.0 <8` and services
`>=13.0.0 <14` are unchanged. This patch changes package metadata only.

entries.title: @alia-codea/cli 3.0.2
@alia.onl/sdk 22.0.0
entries.content:
Requires `@oxy.so/core >=7.1.0 <8` and `@oxy.so/services >=13.0.0 <14`.
Text, dictation, speech and voice use the shared account transport. Account
switches and sign-out invalidate pending work; websocket credentials are
refreshed through the shared origin-bound getter before connecting. Own Oxy
apps use their current account without app scopes or consent. External
credentials retain their existing limits.

entries.title: @alia.onl/server 1.2.0
entries.content:
Adds `createAliaForOxyService` and `createAliaTransportForOxyService` for
Oxy workload transport with Alia’s canonical audience and verified requester
context. The `./internal` entry shares the authenticated API/gateway protocol
without importing React or a server SDK through the client entry. Existing
external credential clients remain supported.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.5.3
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **Every entry type-checks on its own.** `@alia.onl/sdk/text`, `/ask`, `/ask/text` and `/voice`
  reach components that use NativeWind's `className`, but only the root entry carried
  `/// <reference types="nativewind/types" />`. Expo apps load NativeWind's types themselves and
  never noticed; a consumer that does not (a Vite app) got 65 `className` errors importing
  `@alia.onl/sdk/text`. Each of those entries now carries the reference.
- `@alia.onl/sdk/avatar` no longer needs the host to declare Node's `process`: the one
  `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_ALIA_API_URL` read declares its own type (Metro still inlines it).

### Added

- `check:entry-types` (in `prepublishOnly` and CI): compiles a consumer of each entry in
  `exports` alone, through a real `node_modules` link, with nothing loaded globally and the
  strictest consumer's options.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.5.2
entries.content:
### Fixed

- Welcome and conversation sheets grow and shrink with their content up to Bloom’s
  available-height limit, instead of filling the entire frame. Bloom owns the Screen
  sizing, scrolling, keyboard clearance and safe areas.
- The empty thread no longer adds composer clearance a second time. Growing and
  shrinking a draft now changes the sheet height by the composer’s actual change.

### Changed

- The Bloom peer is `>=15.10.1 <16.0.0`, which provides intrinsic Screen sizing
  inside content-sized sheets and clips decorative chat backgrounds.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.5.0
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **The SDK no longer ships every Oxy account screen to the app.** The host's app assertion
  (`useAppAssertion`) was read from `@oxy.so/services/ui`, the only entry that exported it, and
  that entry registers every account screen at import (with Bloom's phone flags and the rest), so
  every app using the SDK carried them in its first-paint JS: +0.58 MiB in CrowdSource's reviewer.
  It now comes from the lean `@oxy.so/services/ui/client`, like `useOxy` and `useAuth`.
  `check:entries` refuses `@oxy.so/services/ui` from every entry, as it already refused the root.

### Changed

- The `@oxy.so/services` peer is `>=12.1.0`, the first release whose `ui/client` exports
  `useAppAssertion`.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.4.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`@alia.onl/sdk/text` and `@alia.onl/sdk/ask/text`: the chat without bundling the voice
  call.** `voice={false}` hid the call, but its code still shipped: since 21.3.2 the web build
  inlines the call into the chat's chunk, so a text-only app paid for it. The new entries export
  the same `AliaChatSheet`, `AliaChatScreen` and `AliaChatContent`, and `AliaAskProvider` /
  `useAskAgent` with a lazily loaded sheet. None of them reaches the call's modules (its socket,
  protocol and audio engine), and they never offer a call. Read-aloud and dictation stay.
  CrowdSource's reviewer, which switched `AliaChatSheet` to `@alia.onl/sdk/text`: lazy sheet
  chunk 1,455,831 → 1,357,287 bytes (413.8 → 374.2 KB gzip), `__common.js` 3,978,158 →
  3,962,370 bytes, no new chunk. The README has a table of which entry to import.

### Changed

- `AliaChatContent` no longer imports the call. It draws whatever call `VoiceCallContext` hands it,
  and the root entry and `@alia.onl/sdk/ask` export their chat through `withVoiceCall`, so those
  two behave as before. `check:entries` checks that the text entries never reach the call, on any
  platform, and draw no async boundary on web other than the ask sheet's.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.3.2
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **On web the SDK draws no async chunk boundary of its own**, so an app that lazy-loads its Alia
  sheet keeps the chat in that chunk instead of its first paint. Expo's Metro serializer hoists
  every module two async chunks share into `__common.js`, loaded at first paint; the SDK's own
  `import()` calls (the call's `VoiceSession`, the root entry's `AliaAskProvider` sheet, the
  `expo-audio`, document-picker and image readers) made such chunks inside the app's, and moved the
  whole chat and the Bloom it draws with into `__common.js`. On web those now import statically
  (`.web` forks); native keeps its lazy loads. The root entry's `AliaAskProvider` imports its sheet
  statically on every platform (the root already holds the chat); `@alia.onl/sdk/ask` keeps its
  one lazy boundary. CrowdSource's reviewer: first-paint JS 1.57 MiB gzip → 1.23 MiB, largest
  file 5.05 MiB → 3.79 MiB, its lazy Alia chunk 29 KiB → 404 KiB gzip. `check:entries` holds it.
- **The source compiles under `erasableSyntaxOnly`.** The SDK ships TypeScript source, and a
  consumer that compiles it with `erasableSyntaxOnly` (OxyHQ/website, `tsc -b`) failed with TS1294
  on two constructor parameter properties in `runtime/conversations.ts`
  (`ConversationNotFoundError.conversationId`, the offline store). They are now declared fields
  assigned in the constructor, and the SDK's own `tsconfig.json` sets `erasableSyntaxOnly`, so
  `typecheck` (CI and `prepublishOnly`) refuses parameter properties, enums and namespaces.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.3.1
entries.content:
- Ask Alia follows the active account language resolved by Oxy Services instead of defaulting to
  English. Changes to that language update the open sheet without replacing its conversation.
- Ship a complete Spanish chat catalogue, including composer, voice, menus, thought panel and
  conversation errors. Regional Spanish tags use it; host label overrides remain supported.
- Apply the sheet's labels above its hooks and all its sheets, so sharing errors and the thought
  panel use the same language as the conversation.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.3.0
entries.content:
The SDK runs on Expo SDK 58 (React Native 0.88, React 19.3) as well as Expo 57.

### Changed

- **Peers admit Expo SDK 58.** Every `expo-*` peer is `^57.0.0 || ^58.0.0`, `react-native` is
  `^0.86.0 || ^0.88.0` and `react-native-gesture-handler` `^2.32.0 || ^3.3.0` (SDK 58 ships 3.3).
  `@oxy.so/bloom` is `>=10.21.0`, the first Bloom whose `TextInput` ref props type-check under
  React Native 0.88's strict TypeScript API.

### Fixed

- **A picked image is read with `expo-file-system`'s `File` API** (`new File(uri).base64()`). The
  root entry's `readAsStringAsync` is the legacy API, which throws at runtime since the package
  moved it to `expo-file-system/legacy`, so attaching a photo on iOS or Android failed.
- **An edit and a regenerate call `AliaRuntimeHost.onTurnStart`**, like a send from the composer
  or a retry: each sends a new turn. A host that judges what a turn does against the moment it
  was sent (a host tool's staleness check) used to judge an edited or regenerated turn against the
  turn before it. An edit that sends nothing (an unknown message, empty content) calls nothing.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.2.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`parseCatalogueTool` and `toolRendererKey` from `@alia.onl/sdk/tools`.** Which app a tool call
  belongs to (`oxy_<app>__<tool>` / `self_<app>__<tool>`) is now readable without loading React
  Native, so a host's own pure models and tests — the code that decides what a screen shows —
  can tell its catalogue's results apart. The main entry exports the same two functions as before.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 21.1.0
entries.content:
A shared conversation has one address, Alia's, whichever app minted it (`docs/agent-embedding.md`
§6).

### Added

- **`url` on `AliaConversationShare`**: `useShareConversation().share` (and a host's `onShare`)
  gets the link to hand on, `https://alia.onl/shared/<token>`, rather than a token to build its own
  page around.
- **`aliaSharedConversationUrl(token)`**: the same link, for an app that redirects the share links
  it minted before to Alia's page.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 20.2.0
entries.content:
An app mounts its one sheet at the root without the chat in its entry bundle.

### Added

- **`@alia.onl/sdk/ask`**, a leaf entry with `AliaAskProvider` and `useAskAgent` alone. The root
  entry still exports both, but brings the whole chat with them.

### Changed

- **`AliaAskProvider` loads its sheet lazily** (`components/AliaAskSheet.tsx`, one `import()`) and
  mounts it on the first `ask`. Signed in, the module is fetched in the background, so the first
  `ask` does not wait on the network. `check:entries` holds that `./ask` loads none of the chat
  with the entry.
- **Ref and event types are React Native 0.88-ready.** A ref to a `ScrollView` or `TextInput` is
  typed `ComponentRef<typeof …>` (0.88 types both as function components), and key presses are
  `TextInputKeyPressEvent` (`TextInputKeyPressEventData` is deprecated since 0.86). Nothing
  changes on 0.86. The peer ranges stay on Expo 57 / React Native 0.86: Bloom's own `TextInput`
  ref props are not 0.88-ready yet.

irm https://get.tnp.network/ps | iex

`docs/architecture/security.md` §7. Build provenance:

entries.title: TNP Client v0.2.0
entries.content:
TNP Client v0.2.0 — overlay network with encrypted tunnels

**Install (one command):**
```bash
# macOS / Linux
curl -fsSL https://get.tnp.network | sh

# Windows (PowerShell)
irm https://get.tnp.network/ps | iex
```

**Platforms:** linux-x64, linux-arm64, darwin-x64, darwin-arm64, windows-x64

**What's new:**
- Interactive CLI menu (`tnp` with no args)
- Overlay network: SOCKS5 proxy + encrypted WebSocket tunnels
- Service node mode (`tnp serve`)
- Become a relay node from the menu
- Cross-platform installer scripts
